#54751. Study: Sign-In Problems Are Primary Drivers of Help Desk Tickets

📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (414 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thejournal ↗ Open Full Page

Study: Sign-In Problems Are Primary Drivers of Help Desk Tickets

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (414 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thejournal

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sign-in problems account for up to 53% of help desk tickets at individual enterprises, but network challenges can take significantly longer to resolve, according to a new study from ControlUp.
  • Analyzing 1,069,110 help desk tickets, the IT operations tech giant identified password resets, account lockouts, and multifactor authentication (MFA) challenges as major drivers of support demand.
  • In a recent development, at one large enterprise, account-related tickets took a median of 11 minutes to resolve, compared with 50 hours for network problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sign-in problems account for up to 53% of help desk tickets at individual enterprises, but network challenges can take significantly longer to resolve, according to a new study from ControlUp.

Analyzing 1,069,110 help desk tickets, the IT operations tech giant identified password resets, account lockouts, and multifactor authentication (MFA) challenges as major drivers of support demand.

In a recent development, at one large enterprise, account-related tickets took a median of 11 minutes to resolve, compared with 50 hours for network problems. Meanwhile, 87% of network and phone tickets were reassigned between teams, compared with 20% of account tickets.

Industry observers note that MFA enrollment and re-enrollment problems appeared at 40% of organizations, with one in five linking these concerns to employees replacing or upgrading their phones. Virtual desktop problems appeared at 55% of organizations analyzed.

Traditional phone support remained a major channel for IT assistance.

Among organizations that recorded how support requests were submitted, 57% reported that phone calls accounted for approximately two-thirds or more of contacts. At one organization, that figure reached 99%.

Industry observers note that machine-generated tickets from monitoring, security, backup, and patching systems appeared at half of the organizations studied. At 15%, automated tickets represented between 25% and 50% of all requests.

The research covered enterprises across retail, healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, construction, energy, and IT services.

ControlUp remarked the findings highlight the need to evaluate recurring problems and their operational impact rather than relying solely on ticket volume and resolution speed.

"IT organizations have traditionally measured support performance by how quickly they close tickets, but that doesn't tell the whole story," said Simon Townsend, senior vice president of marketing and office of the CTO at ControlUp.

"A password reset that takes a few minutes and an infrastructure failure that disrupts an entire location shouldn't carry the same operational weight.".

For more information, go to the ControlUp site.

AI-powered vulnerability research is contributing to a major increase in security updates, raising concerns that IT teams could fall behind as patching demands grow, according to cybersecurity company ThreatDown.

Unauthorized artificial intelligence tools and agents are creating security risks for organizations as AI adoption increases, according to cybersecurity company Sophos.

In its latest threat intelligence report, Ontinue found that attackers are increasingly using trusted workplace tools to trick owners into giving them access to enterprise networks.

A vendor coalition built on an Okta-developed blueprint is proposing a shared architecture for discovering, governing, monitoring, and containing enterprise AI agents.

#54744. Enterprise AI Spending Outpaces Adoption Growth, Report Finds

📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (667 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 Thejournal ↗ Open Full Page

Enterprise AI Spending Outpaces Adoption Growth, Report Finds

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (667 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a new Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.
  • In a recent development, the venture capital firm's 2026 State of Enterprise AI report estimates deployment spending reached a $176.8 billion annualized run rate by September, up from $33 billion in 2025.
  • A larger bill can reflect broader use inside an organization, but it does not independently establish that the additional work is useful or profitable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Enterprise AI spending is growing faster than the number of organizations paying for it, according to a new Menlo Ventures report that points to a shift from buying access for employees to financing work performed by agents.

In a recent development, the venture capital firm's 2026 State of Enterprise AI report estimates deployment spending reached a $176.8 billion annualized run rate by September, up from $33 billion in 2025. The share of enterprises paying for AI rose from 55% to 65%.

A larger bill can reflect broader use inside an organization, but it does not independently establish that the additional work is useful or profitable.

Menlo's methodology describes revenue figures as annualized run rates. The $176.8 billion estimate therefore should not be read as $176.8 billion already spent during the first nine months of 2026.

The report also distinguishes unusually heavy spenders from the typical respondent. Average reported spending reached 4.7 times the prior year's level, while the median reached 2.2 times. That gap suggests a smaller group of large spenders drove the average substantially.

The practical implication is that an industry growth figure may be a poor benchmark for an individual organization's budget. Buyers need to understand their own workload growth and the results it produces.

"Agents are changing the economics of software," Menlo principal Derek Xiao remarked in the firm's announcement.

In a recent development, menlo reports that agents account for 80% of tokens on OpenRouter, a service providing access to multiple models. That measures activity on one platform, rather than all enterprise AI use. Token consumption also measures processing volume, rather than completed business outcomes.

In a recent development, an agent that makes repeated attempts can consume more resources without delivering proportionately more value. For procurement teams, the relevant comparison is consequently the cost of completing acceptable work, including the review it requires.

It has been revealed that menlo estimates that Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google capture 69% of enterprise AI deployment spending. That measure is distinct from their shares of enterprise language-model API spending, a narrower category. The figures should not be used interchangeably.

The report draws on a Morning Consult survey of nearly 400 U.S. enterprise decision-makers responsible for more than $4 billion in AI spending. Market totals are modeled estimates informed by surveys, public filings, and third-party reports. Menlo discloses investments in Anthropic and OpenRouter.

A separate announcement from Information Services Group describes buyers putting more emphasis on the economics and reliability of production deployments. ISG says ongoing security and observability work remains necessary as organizations scale.

That provides a useful distinction between market demand and business value. Suppliers can generate growing revenue while customers still determine which deployments justify the cost.

According to recent reports, for enterprise leaders, the latest spending estimate strengthens the case for examining usage beyond license counts. It leaves the harder purchasing question with the customer: How much worthwhile work did the increased spending actually buy?

Menlo's State of Enterprise AI report is available here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it’s an established social etiquette rule that showing up to a party empty-handed is a bit of a faux pas. Of course, there are more intimate gatherings where a simple bottle of wine or an extra cheese for the board will suffice, but the holiday season runs on a different track. Homes are dressed to the nines, menus are calibrated to merrier flavors, and the stakes somehow feel higher. Arriving with a gift for the hostess not only signals your appreciation, but also adds to the evening’s celebratory air. But what to bring?

Recent findings suggest that there’s zero shame in going the traditional route—no one is going to turn their nose up at a Le Labo candle, after all. If your host is a hardcore holiday enthusiast, why not bring a handcrafted ornament to dress their tree with? Or a fresh stack of illustrated Christmas cards? Something pretty for the pantry will always go to great use, and if you have a strong sense of their taste in interiors, a sleek vase or decorative tray will surely make your host feel extra special.

In a recent development, this year, rather than scrambling to secure the best hostess gifts in the 11th hour, save yourself the stress and stock up ahead of time. Below, shop over 75 picks (starting at just $12) to bring along to all your upcoming holiday fêtes.

Phishing Threats Totaled 7.3 Billion in Q3 2026

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (462 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thejournal

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • E-mail phishing threats reached 7.3 billion in Q3 2026, with September activity increasing 41% from August, according to Microsoft Threat Intelligence.
  • According to a report from Microsoft Threat Intelligence and the Microsoft Defender Security Research Team, phishing detections reached nearly 3 billion in September alone.
  • The findings also highlighted changes in attacker techniques, including business-service impersonation, credential theft, and social engineering through Microsoft Teams.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

E-mail phishing threats reached 7.3 billion in Q3 2026, with September activity increasing 41% from August, according to Microsoft Threat Intelligence.

According to a report from Microsoft Threat Intelligence and the Microsoft Defender Security Research Team, phishing detections reached nearly 3 billion in September alone.

The findings also highlighted changes in attacker techniques, including business-service impersonation, credential theft, and social engineering through Microsoft Teams.

The Redmond-based firm recognized approximately 129 million malicious messages spoofing the sender domains of tracked business services during Q3.

It has been revealed that docuSign was the most frequently spoofed brand in September, accounting for 29% of the month's tracked spoofing activity. Adobe, SurveyMonkey, and Barracuda also experienced increases toward the end of the quarter.

The research found that some malicious messages were delivered despite failing e-mail authentication checks and being identified as threats.

In September, tenant- or user-level security overrides applied to 63% of these messages with a recorded security outcome — most involved tenant-level exceptions.

Microsoft warned that overly broad exceptions intended to support legitimate business communications can weaken protection against impersonation attacks.

The company emphasized that these findings do not establish whether recipients opened the messages or whether accounts were compromised.

Microsoft also recorded approximately 141,000 malicious Teams call attempts during Q3.

Attackers increasingly used ordinary personal names instead of explicitly impersonating IT support personnel. Such display names accounted for 46% of an observed sample in July, rising to 88% in September.

Meanwhile, QR code phishing declined 67% compared to Q2, totaling roughly 12.1 million attacks.

CAPTCHA-gated phishing activity increased toward the end of the quarter, reaching 3.1 million detected attacks in September. SVG attachments played a significant role in the increase.

Credential theft remained the primary objective of malicious attachment campaigns, with approximately 94% to 96% of payload-based attacks directing customers to phishing sites or fraudulent sign-in pages.

Microsoft recommended reviewing Exchange Online Protection and Defender for Office 365 configurations, enabling Safe Links and Safe Attachments, and strengthening authentication protections.

The company also advised organizations to review security exceptions and verify the identities of external Teams contacts before responding to suspicious requests.

For more information, go to the Microsoft blog post.

AI-powered vulnerability research is contributing to a major increase in security updates, raising concerns that IT teams could fall behind as patching demands grow, according to cybersecurity manufacturer ThreatDown.

Unauthorized artificial intelligence tools and agents are creating security risks for organizations as AI adoption increases, according to cybersecurity tech giant Sophos.

In its latest threat intelligence report, Ontinue found that attackers are increasingly using trusted workplace tools to trick consumers into giving them access to enterprise networks.

A vendor coalition built on an Okta-developed blueprint is proposing a shared architecture for discovering, governing, monitoring, and containing enterprise AI agents.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • There’s something undeniably chic about a head of long, luscious hair.
  • As hair matures, however, maintaining the same level of shine, strength, and vitality can require more attention.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

There’s something undeniably chic about a head of long, luscious hair. Think glossy, waist-skimming, bouncy, voluminous lengths that make extensions an option rather than a long-term commitment. What’s more, long hair provides the ultimate canvas for experimentation, with styling possibilities that feel limitless.

As hair matures, however, maintaining the same level of shine, strength, and vitality can require more attention. As texture changes and dryness increases, the key is to adapt your routine to give your longer lengths the care they deserve. “Long hair can look beautiful at any age, but keeping mature hair glossy and healthy-looking is all about replenishing moisture and maintaining shine,” indicates celebrity hairstylist Naomi Brooks. “I always recommend prioritising hydrating products that help smooth the hair cuticle, improve softness, and enhance shine, alongside regular trims to keep the lengths and ends looking healthy.”.

Sources indicate that if you’re considering making the transition and letting your bob grow out, look to a host of celebrities for inspiration. From Demi Moore and Naomi Campbell to Andie MacDowell and Claudia Schiffer, countless iterations are proving just how effortless long hair can look on women over 50. As Brooks explains: “Demi Moore is a fantastic example of how beautiful long hair can look at any age. Her hair is consistently glossy, healthy-looking, and full of movement.”.

While genetics certainly play a role, Moore’s glossy lengths are also the result of great care and strategic products. Her hairstylist, Dimitris Giannetos, revealed on social media that he often relies on Kérastase’s Gloss Absolu Glaze Drops Anti-Frizz Hair Oil to reduce frizz, boost shine, and ensure hair remains sleek without looking too heavy. Indeed, experts recommend investing in a high-quality hydrating treatment to ensure mature hair is treated with extra care. “Mature hair can become drier, finer or more fragile over time, so maintaining moisture and shine is important,” states Warren Edwards, creative director at Warren & the Hare.

In a recent development, additionally, for those with gray or silver hair, session stylist Danilo Giangreco recommends incorporating a clear gloss into your routine to enhance shine. This can also help counteract any unwanted brassiness, ensuring hair appears brighter and healthier.

In a recent development, another expert-approved tip is to keep heat styling to a minimum where possible. If you do rely on hot tools, applying heat protectant can help shield strands from damage while preserving moisture, strength, and shine.

Finally, contrary to popular belief, long hair thrives on regular maintenance. Though it may seem counterintuitive when trying to grow your hair, routine appointments are essential to keep split ends at bay and prevent the ends from looking too thin or tired. In turn, this helps keep long, mature hair looking fuller, healthier, and overall more glossy.

Industry News: These Are the Home Trends Gaining Ground for 2027, According to Zillow

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (700 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Above: A color-drenched den on Long Island, New York, designed by General Assembly.
  • Homes are getting smarter, but sellers are also advertising places to unplug.
  • The report tracks year-over-year changes in mentions of hundreds of features across millions of for-sale listings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Above: A color-drenched den on Long Island, New York, designed by General Assembly.

Homes are getting smarter, but sellers are also advertising places to unplug. Zillow’s 2027 Home Trends Report finds growing mentions of both AI and tech-free spaces, along with color-drenched rooms, home offices, and “catios.”.

The report tracks year-over-year changes in mentions of hundreds of features across millions of for-sale listings. The results reflect how sellers and agents are marketing homes—not a survey of buyers or evidence that a particular feature will help a property sell. Still, they offer a look at the amenities and design details increasingly making their way into listing descriptions. Here are the main takeaways.

Mentions of AI are up 119 percent, the largest increase in this year’s report. Zillow points to AI-powered appliances among the features sellers are advertising, while mentions of app-controlled home systems rose 34 percent.

Spaces to unplug are also appearing 34 percent more often. The report describes an interest in both technology that simplifies daily tasks and designated places to take a break from it.

“Digital detox is the upcoming luxury,” says Amanda Pendleton, Zillow’s home trends expert, in a statement. “Homes are getting smarter, but buyers also want tech-free zones where nothing needs charging. Sellers and their real estate agents are now highlighting spaces to unplug.”.

Color-drenched spaces—rooms where the same color extends across the walls, ceiling, and trim—are up 84 percent in listing mentions, making them one of the report’s biggest increases. Zillow sees the approach as part of a move toward bolder, more polished interiors. Exterior finishes are gaining ground, too: painted brick is up 27 percent, and board-and-batten siding rose 24 percent.

Recent findings suggest that color drenching takes a shade beyond the walls and onto the ceiling, trim, and other architectural details. The approach has even spawned a bathroom variation: tile drenching, which extends the same tile across surfaces for a continuous look.

Sources indicate that the language used to describe these homes is changing alongside the features. Mentions of “elevated” rose 71 percent, while “cozy” fell 22 percent, “eclectic” dropped 19 percent, and “boho” declined 13 percent. Cozy remains one of the most common words in listings, but it’s appearing less frequently than it did a year ago.

Home offices are up 42 percent, media rooms are up 37 percent, and flex spaces are up 35 percent. Open-concept layouts, meanwhile, are holding steady. The findings don’t point to the end of the open floor proposal, but they do show more listings advertising places for work, entertainment, exercise, and privacy.

Kitchen language is moving in the other direction. Mentions of “chef’s kitchens” fell 21 percent, and “gourmet kitchens” declined 15 percent.

Mentions of multigenerational living jumped 58 percent. Zillow connects the increase to homes accommodating the “sandwich generation,” or people caring for children and older family members.

Features that can serve different ages and needs are also appearing more frequently. Grab bars are up 18 percent, wider doorways are up 13 percent, and nurseries rose 9 percent. The report places these changes alongside the growing emphasis on flexible rooms and spaces with more than one use.

It has been revealed that the home spa is changing. Mentions of spa-inspired bathrooms rose 60 percent, and cold plunge pools increased 44 percent. Jacuzzis and jetted tubs, meanwhile, each fell about 9 percent.

Sources indicate that spaces for exercise are also gaining ground. Home gyms are up 18 percent, while golf simulators rose 29 percent. Together, the findings cover both workout spaces and amenities marketed around rest and recovery, rather than a single version of the home wellness room.

Cats get a category of their own this year. “Catios”—screened-in outdoor spaces that let indoor cats spend time outside—are appearing in 32 percent more listings. A place to get some air, watch the birds, and keep an eye on the neighbors—the cat has a wish list, too.

Breaking: Brace Yourselves, Another Harlan Coben Netflix Drama Is on the Way

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (323 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You will not be surprised to hear that Netflix’s favorite crime-thriller maestro has had yet another commission.
  • Netflix has just revealed that it’s working on a new adaptation of Coben’s The Innocent, led by the same creative team behind I Will Find You.
  • According to recent reports, the story revolves around a man named Matt Hunter, who tries to live a quiet life with his wife, Olivia, in Upcoming Jersey while concealing secrets from his mysterious past.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You will not be surprised to hear that Netflix’s favorite crime-thriller maestro has had yet another commission. Myron Bolitar hasn’t even finished filming, but news has arrived that another Harlan Coben joint has been green-lit.

Netflix has just revealed that it’s working on a new adaptation of Coben’s The Innocent, led by the same creative team behind I Will Find You. The novel was previously adapted as a Spanish-language series, also for Netflix, but this adaptation promises a fresh, dynamic spin on the hit story. Read on for everything we know so far about The Innocent.

According to recent reports, the story revolves around a man named Matt Hunter, who tries to live a quiet life with his wife, Olivia, in Upcoming Jersey while concealing secrets from his mysterious past. When he and Olivia try to buy a house in his hometown, those secrets start to spill out and, worse, people start turning up dead.

Soon enough, Matt becomes the prime suspect in the murders, leaving him and Olivia to do everything they can to prove his innocence, clear his name, and protect their future together.

Industry observers note that as the show has only just been announced, we don’t have any details of the cast yet. But Cole Galvin, Netflix’s vice president of drama series, remarked, “Harlan Coben is one of the great creative partnerships at Netflix, and The Innocent marks our 15th story together. Nobody builds a can’t-look-away thriller like Harlan, and Robert Hull, Bryan Wynbrandt and Steven Lilied brought their own dynamic creativity to I Will Find You, a global hit for us. We’re thrilled to welcome them to the Netflix family, and we can’t wait for the world to get hooked on their Innocent.”.

There’s no information about the show’s release date, and we imagine there won’t be for a while, as there are still two other Coben novel adaptations in production at the streamer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a woman who writes about men's fashion, guys I meet on dating apps love to ask me what jeans to buy—and I always recommend Levi’s. Specifically, Levi’s 505 jeans. “Not 501s?” one asked frantically. As Luke Guillory, Esquire’s commerce editor, poignantly noted in his Levi’s denim guide, the fit and materials of Levi’s infamous 501s have changed over the years, and “the most straightforward Levi's fit is not that straightforward, nor is it consistent across era.” By comparison, the slightly more modern 505 cut is a safer bet, especially when shopping online during Black Friday.

Industry observers note that “I prefer my jeans to hug up top, drape down low. A 505 does that,” Guillory wrote, declaring them Esquire’s pick for the best men’s jeans. “They're universally flattering and classic cut, so you don't have to worry about them going out of style. As a cheap pair of jeans go, it's the best way to go.”.

Industry observers note that like many good things, Levi’s 505 jeans are on sale for Black Friday and Cyber Monday. This year, the brand’s entire site (minus a few exclusions) will be 40 percent off from November 23 to December 1, with early access starting November 19 for Red Tab Members. While you can find Levi’s markdowns at Amazon and other major retailers, you’ll find the widest range of washes, inseam lengths, and specialized fits by going straight to the source.

If you haven’t yet, it’s worth shopping Levi’s beyond jeans. The Sherpa Trucker Esquire editors have relied on for years now comes in a fresh corduroy fabric. For reliable workwear pants, try the rugged 568 Carpenter. And don’t sleep on Levi’s Classic Western Denim Shirt, which also makes a great gift.

Below are more of my top sale picks from the brand.

#54703. Movado’s New Tempo-Matic Watch Is Inspired by an Iconic Piece from the ’70s

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (276 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

Movado’s New Tempo-Matic Watch Is Inspired by an Iconic Piece from the ’70s

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (276 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Movado was founded in 1881 in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, which isn’t a particularly odd backstory for a heritage Swiss watch brand.
  • Right now, a growing band of horological nerds is finding rich pickings in the Movado back catalog and pushing up vintage prices considerably—especially for its mid-century chronographs and its legendary Museum Watch (which celebrates 80 years in 2027; more of that to come) in the process.
  • According to recent reports, it’s not only the collectors who are digging into Movado’s past, however.

Movado was founded in 1881 in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, which isn’t a particularly odd backstory for a heritage Swiss watch brand. But it has been American owned since 1983 and has a distinct quality tied deeply to its long history in the U.S. market—which puts it slightly outside the predictable purview of many watch collectors.

Right now, a growing band of horological nerds is finding rich pickings in the Movado back catalog and pushing up vintage prices considerably—especially for its mid-century chronographs and its legendary Museum Watch (which celebrates 80 years in 2027; more of that to come) in the process.

According to recent reports, it’s not only the collectors who are digging into Movado’s past, however. Last month, the brand released the Heritage Tempo-Matic ($995–$1,095), a re-creation of a watch that merges sporty and retro design in a neat and slinky package. The Tempo-Matic, Movado’s first automatic movement, was launched in 1945 and went on to power a broad range of Movado’s wristwatches. But the rounded yet boxy “TV” shape of the new Heritage Tempo-Matic is unmistakably 1970s, when watch design took a giant leap forward into sexy new territory.

The 2026 version is available in three executions, each powered by the reliable Sellita SW200-1B movement and fitted with integrated steel bracelets that positively scream seventies. Two of them come in brushed steel with vertically brushed burgundy or blue dials. A third—which, we must admit, is our favorite—is gold-tone PVD with a warm gray dial. You’d be hard-pressed to find such an elegant, authentic, and affordable homage to the 1970s—a decade that’s currently a very hot motif in watch-collecting circles—anywhere else.

Latest Update: The 63 Best New Perfumes and Fragrances of 2026

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1523 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that everything smells like vanilla.
  • But hundreds of other fragrance debuts in 2026 deserve a spot on your vanity and a spritz on your skin, and many are far less sweet.
  • See all the winners of the 2026 Harper’s Bazaar Fragrance Awards, plus quotes from our beauty editors on what makes these formulas worthy of your next blind buy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that everything smells like vanilla. At least, that’s what perfume naysayers will tell you. And it’s somewhat true: If you’re judging by what’s popular, ubiquitous, or cool with the youth, then sure—vanilla scents and sweet gourmands are still trending.

But hundreds of other fragrance debuts in 2026 deserve a spot on your vanity and a spritz on your skin, and many are far less sweet. Gourmands took a turn for the weird and fruity this year, with notes like lychee and rice milk popping up in otherwise innocuous formulas. Woods and ambers continued to reign, as did spice-forward and citrus scents with unexpected depth. Perfumers are meeting our demand for newness in increasingly interesting, artistic ways, and we smelled hundreds of their creations to choose the 63 winners of our annual fragrance awards.

See all the winners of the 2026 Harper’s Bazaar Fragrance Awards, plus quotes from our beauty editors on what makes these formulas worthy of your next blind buy.

Chanel Coco Mademoiselle Crush Absolu.

“Perfumer Olivier Polge reinvented the beloved “Coco Mad” scent as Crush Absolu, a latest juice centered around patchouli, amber, rose, and a lychee-grapefruit accord. ‘There’s something voluptuous, something very prideful, something very addictive,’ Polge indicates about the new scent.”.

According to recent reports, “The new iteration of J’adore was inspired by Rihanna herself. As such, it’s a sweeter, bolder take, with notes of honeyed jasmine, rose, ylang-ylang, and vanilla.” —JR.

Guerlain L'Heure Bleue Eau de Parfum.

"Bazaar’s Beauty Commerce Editor, Tiffany Dodson Davis, describes Guerlain’s L’Heure Bleue Eau de Parfum as the “scent of sunset,” thanks to a blue-sky accord that evokes the moment the sun goes down and the air turns crisp, clean, and fresh." —KI.

Burberry Goddess Amber Vanilla Eau de Parfum Intense.

“Lavender, maple syrup, four vanilla notes—I feel like a dog hearing all my favorite words. The result is a warm, ambery gourmand perfume that’s perfect for the cooler months.” —JR.

Armani Beauty Emporio Armani Power of You Eau de Parfum.

It has been revealed that "Passionfruit adds an unexpected zing to the vanilla base here, making Power of You one of our favorite tropical-leaning gourmands of the year. It's pure summertime sex appeal." —JR.

“Henry Rose Ripe captures fruits—from lychee to watermelon—at their juiciest, ripest point, like a delectable first bite, before packing a punch with black pepper, cardamom, and powdery florals.” —Katie Intner, beauty market and commerce editor.

Influxious Magic Hour Eau de Parfum.

“One of the most unexpected fruity florals on the list, Influxious Magic Hour melds watermelon and dragon fruit with spicy chili pepper for a burst of juicy energy.” —KI.

Balmain Paris Destin De Balmain Eau de Parfum.

In a recent development, "The opening note of Destin is strawberry, a modern and sweet fruity note that swiftly dries down to a patchouli-forward, gorgeous floral musk. It will make you smell expensive." —JR.

According to recent reports, "Neroli, bergamot, and yuzu combine with notes of orange blossom, jasmine, and tonka bean for a well-rounded fragrance that stands out from the pack. Parfum de Marly's Athénaïs eau de parfum has a zesty composition upon first spritz before drying down to a powdery finish." —Tiffany Dodson Davis, beauty commerce editor.

“Gap recently brought back its iconic fragrance line from the ’90s, including the nostalgic Grass Eau de Parfum. It now features matcha, vetiver, green mandarin, and cedar for a fresh take on its outdoorsy, earthy scent.” —KI.

Maison Francis Kurkdjian Oud Velvet Mood Extrait de Parfum.

Recent findings suggest that “For those who are oud-averse, Maison Francis Kurkdjian’s Oud Velvet Mood is a lighter iteration of the category. The oud has a woody quality, and when paired with spicy cinnamon, rich saffron, and juicy peach, the result is light and warm like the sun.” —KI.

“This stunning perfume is all gardenia and vanilla, and in its simplicity, it happens to be one of our most complimented scents of the year.” —JR.

Balenciaga Pink Oud Extrait de Parfum.

Industry observers note that "This is a bold, long-wearing scent for those who live and die for the sensual pairing of rose and oud. We're obsessed with the way it blooms and evolves on skin throughout the night." —JR.

Ex Nihilo Demon Dancer Eau de Parfum.

“Ex Nihilo Demon Dancer feels like moving through the crisp air on a spring day, with peppermint providing a breezy contrast to juicy rhubarb, bright bergamot, and warm tonka bean.” —KI.

“We don’t know what we love more: the magnetic floral perfume that begs to be worn every day, the sculptural bottle, or the bookish packaging that made us a fan before we even took our first whiff.” —JR.

“You can’t go wrong with Beyoncé’s sultry and sophisticated hair perfume, which leaves hair with a long-wearing trail of bergamot, jasmine, oud, sandalwood, and Haitian vetiver.” —JR.

Creed Iris Debonair Eau de Parfum.

Sources indicate that “Delightfully unisex, this aromatic scent is a masterclass in balance. The top opens with bergamot, cardamom, pink pepper, and wormwood. In the middle, you’ll find fruity fig, lavender, and violet leaf. The base is iris, amberwood, and ambrette.” —JR.

D.S. & Durga Resurrected Corpse Flower.

“Earthy and green, with an olive top note and banana base note—this is the perfume to buy this year if you want to smell wholly original and unabashedly cool.” —JR.

In a recent development, “Creamy and warm with notes of chocolate and coffee, this is the must-have gourmand perfume of the winter. In a word, it makes us feel happy.” —JR.

Discothèque Next to Me or Nothing Eau De Parfum.

“More of a feeling than a fragrance, this scent is airy and easy to wear, with breezy notes of milk, jasmine, and woods.” —JR.

Phlur Heavy Cream Eau de Parfum.

"Gourmand lovers will want to overindulge in this elevated eau de parfum, which combines two types of creams—whipped and coconut—along with jasmine blossom and vanilla mousse notes for a sophisticated yet playful olfactory blend." —TDD.

“An olfactory version of a sound bath, Liis Forest Sounds boasts notes of bright yuzu, damp rain (earthier than plain water), green leaves, and woods.” —KI.

Dolce&Gabbana Dolce&Gabbana Your Devotion Eau de Parfum Intense.

"The notes in this fragrance sound good enough to eat: Sicilian lemon, orange blossom, and vanilla milk. This is a date-night, delicious gourmand for those who usually prefer a lighter citrus scent." —JR.

Dries Van Noten Velvet Violet Eau de Parfum.

“This woody-gourmand scent captures the lush texture of velvet with a mix of unusual notes: violet leaf, clary sage essence, toasted sesame, barley roasted, and grilled tonka beans.” —JR.

Ellis Brooklyn Vanilla Rice Eau de Parfum.

According to recent reports, “Rather than wrapping yourself in a cashmere blanket on a cold day, try wearing Ellis Brooklyn’s Vanilla Rice. It combines the warm notes of toasted rice, cherry blossom, sweet vanilla, and creamy coconut milk for a soft, slightly floral scent.” —KI.

Estée Lauder Glimmer Eau de Parfum Spray.

“Estée Lauder’s Glimmer gives crisp orange flower and rose a warm finish with vanilla bean, tonka bean, amber, and two types of wood.” —KI.

Glossier You Soie Eau de Parfum.

“The latest addition to Glossier’s You fragrance lineup, Soie is an aquatic and solar take on a floral scent, with tropical Tiare flower water and creamy rice in place of powdery florals.” —KI.

In a recent development, “Not quite a fragrance, Future Society’s Base Scent is like the no-makeup makeup version of perfume. Infused with prebiotics and a patent-pending technology, the scent is designed to enhance and balance any fragrance layered beneath it—whether that’s lotion, deodorant, or your natural scent—by working with the skin’s microbiome.” —KI.

Harlem Perfume Co. Sensual Muse Eau de Parfum.

“A fruity floral that reads as more sophisticated, Harlem Fragrance Co.’s Sensual Muse gives juicy apricot, bright citrus, and creamy gardenia a warm, compelling character once whipped vanilla, sandalwood, and amber are added into the mix.” —KI.

“If you prefer your cocktails in fragrance form, look no further than By Kilian, which has mastered the art of turning a nutty, warm, slightly sweet espresso martini into a wearable scent that feels especially seductive at night.” —KI.

The MacBook Neo Is on Sale for the First Time Ever

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I am not the first person to point out that MacBooks are expensive.
  • You could buy it for full price and get your money’s worth—although scoring it on sale makes the whole thing even sweeter.
  • Industry observers note that designed as Apple’s answer to the lower-budget laptops running Windows, the Neo’s target audience is technically students—hence the good branding and cool colors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I am not the first person to point out that MacBooks are expensive. I will not be the last. If you monitor this stuff like we do, you’ll have seen the irony that Apple released the budget-conscious MacBook Neo earlier this year—only for the global computing shortage to almost immediately raise the price from $599 to $699.

But the Neo is still cheap. You could buy it for full price and get your money’s worth—although scoring it on sale makes the whole thing even sweeter. Just in time for Black Friday, Amazon shaved $50 off of the buzzy MacBook. Chalk it up to a Christmas miracle.

Industry observers note that designed as Apple’s answer to the lower-budget laptops running Windows, the Neo’s target audience is technically students—hence the good branding and cool colors. That being said, if you need a personal computer for watching Netflix and doing your taxes but don’t want a full desktop, it’s a perfect choice.

The Neo runs on Apple’s A18 Pro chip—the same one that powers the iPhone 16 Pro and Pro Max. If the idea of buying a laptop that runs on a phone chip gives you pause, your stress is better channeled elsewhere. While this isn’t the right device for someone who is planning to run heavy-duty software, it can handle standard Internet browsing, video calls, and the like with ease. Just keep in mind that it has only 8 GB of RAM, so it’s best suited to basic workflows.

Of course, this computer has the added benefit of four jazzy color options: blush and citrus for the bold, indigo for those more subdued, and silver for that classic MacBook aesthetic. Wrapped in an aluminum body with a 13-inch Liquid Retina display, the Neo weighs in at just 2.7 pounds (same as the MacBook Air) and is 0.5 inches thick. (For reference, the iPhone 17 Pro Max is 0.35 inches thick.).

It has been revealed that despite our best efforts, we don’t quite know how Apple determines its deals for big sale events, so there’s no telling if this $50 discount is as good as it’s going to get for Black Friday. In all honesty, we were hoping Amazon would shave $100 off to get the Neo back to its pre-increase price. In our wildest dreams, we’re gunning for a deal that would make this the first-ever sub-$500 MacBook.

According to recent reports, we’re not giving up on a deeper discount once Black Friday proper arrives, but for now the Neo is undoubtedly a smart buy for anyone who wants a laptop that can handle all of the basics. At $649, it’s still a fraction of the cost of the MacBook Air and Pro.

Sources indicate that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Industry observers note that as you might imagine, my coworkers and I, well, we see a crap ton of clothes on a daily basis. We’re fashion editors, after all. Our working hours are spent poring over the latest collections, visiting showrooms to experience the pieces for ourselves, and analyzing every trend. All that remarked, we can be a tough bunch to impress. I mean that earnestly. But when my colleague and I saw a sneak preview of the collaboration between Shopbop’s in-house label, Le Bop, and Julia Berolzheimer, we nearly squealed with delight.

Sources indicate that the collection hits all the right notes. It’s colorful. It’s fun yet sophisticated. And for Berolzheimer, the collaboration felt like a full-circle moment. “I have been a customer of Shopbop since the very beginning of my blog (15 years ago!),” Berolzheimer exclusively told ELLE in an email. “Even back then, Shopbop was a destination for style inspiration and discovery...All of that still holds true for the retailer today. When their design team reached out to me last year to co-design a collection for their private label, Le Bop, it was a no-brainer.”.

Recent findings suggest that the collection features taffeta and satiny fabrics adorned with fringe, tonal animal prints, brocade jackets, and jacquard knits. The rich color palette includes dusty rose, chartreuse, espresso, and ocean blue. It is, I must admit, perfect for party dressing that feels a bit unexpected.

“The inspiration came naturally,” Berolzheimer claims. “It stemmed from my personal style and what I love and want to wear around the holidays. I call my style ‘polished maximalist,’ and the collection is just that. There are some bold statement pieces and coordinating sets, which I love to style together, but you can also wear them separately for a more pared-down look. What I love most about this collection is how you can mix and match the pieces for any festive occasion and continue to style them beyond the holiday season.”.

The Le Bop x Julia Berolzheimer collection is available now on Shopbop.com.

#54695. Inside a Denver Tudor That Blends English Eccentricity With Family-Friendly Design

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1250 w)

Inside a Denver Tudor That Blends English Eccentricity With Family-Friendly Design

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1250 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that when designer Kaitlyn Hoffman and her family returned to the United States after eight years in London, they had grown accustomed to the tighter quarters that city living often dictates.
  • Recent findings suggest that “The biggest design challenge was anticipating how we would actually live in the home,” Hoffman indicates.
  • Recent findings suggest that the nine-month project, which also debuted her firm, Studio Proper Design, restored the home’s Tudor character.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that when designer Kaitlyn Hoffman and her family returned to the United States after eight years in London, they had grown accustomed to the tighter quarters that city living often dictates. Needless to say, settling into a five-bedroom Tudor in Denver’s Cheesman Park neighborhood was a massive leap. Built in 1900, the house was in good condition when Hoffman and her husband bought it, but earlier renovations had left it feeling at odds with its architectural style.

Recent findings suggest that “The biggest design challenge was anticipating how we would actually live in the home,” Hoffman indicates. Because they renovated the space before moving in, she had to guess at everything from where they’d gather to how the house would work for their two young kids. “Ultimately, it was an exercise in designing for a life we hadn’t quite experienced yet and trusting our instincts about how we wanted to live.”.

Recent findings suggest that the nine-month project, which also debuted her firm, Studio Proper Design, restored the home’s Tudor character. Hoffman and her partners at Alter Design + Build gutted the primary and powder bathrooms, overhauled the kitchen, and made smaller updates almost everywhere else. Along the way, plenty of the home’s charming original details got a second life: A pair of French doors found in the basement now anchors a custom pantry, and diamond-pattern mullions in the primary bath windows make the room look as though it had always been part of the house.

It has been revealed that the result is a home that reflects Hoffman’s signature “Brit-ish” style: layered, collected, and not too precious. “I think the magic is in the mix,” she says, crediting her years abroad with inspiring a fondness for eccentricity, coziness, and humor in her design projects. Even the house’s lore fits the mood. Neighbors insist it’s the former home of ‘60s country-rock group Nitty Gritty Dirt Band—though Hoffman admits she’s never been able to confirm it. “Whether it’s true or not, it’s fun to imagine that these walls might have witnessed a little rock-and-roll history.”.

FAST FACTSDesigner: Kaitlyn Hoffman of Studio Proper DesignDesign Partner: Alter Design + BuildStylist: Natalie WaradyLocation: Denver, ColoradoThe Space: A five-bedroom, three-and-a-half-bathroom Tudor across 6,345 square feet.

A place where the whole family gathers and hosts, this living room is packed with personality and beloved furnishings, many of which have changed hands in the family throughout the years. While the decor is decidedly eclectic, the architecture itself is classic and stately. “We wanted this room to have the elegance of a traditional English drawing room, so we introduced egg-and-dart crown molding and a hand-carved Louis XV–style marble fireplace to give the space a greater sense of formality and architectural presence,” Hoffman shares.

According to Hoffman, this area saw a true “everything but the kitchen cabinets” renovation. Existing wall ovens gave way to a freestanding range with a custom hood, and a new pantry took their place. It’s built around a pair of original French doors she found in the basement, adding key storage while hiding away the appliances.

To soften the modern lines, she added a paneled backsplash, unlacquered brass hardware, and sealed walnut butcher block countertops for a warm, rustic touch. “I wanted a kitchen that worked hard for our family but felt every bit as inviting as the rest of the house,” Hoffman adds.

Though the dining room shares space with the living room, both areas needed to have distinct identities. To make guests feel like they’re entering into a completely separate room, Hoffman sourced several statement-making pieces. “I found all six antique Louis-style dining chairs on Facebook Marketplace for just $100, while the mirrored faux-bamboo armoire is a favorite piece we brought back with us from London,” Hoffman claims.

It has been revealed that tucked beneath the stairs between the kitchen and living room is a clever nook for mixing up the drink of the hour. “This multipurpose space houses my husband’s (many!) coffee supplies by day and transforms into a bar by night,” Hoffman says. Like in the kitchen, she preserved the existing cabinetry and gave it a fresh coat of blue paint, upcoming Negresco honed granite countertops, wallpaper, and updated fixtures. Now, it rivals the kitchen as the go-to entertaining spot in the home.

While gut-renovating this powder room, Hoffman fell in love with the botanical wallpaper, and she would’ve covered the entire space in it if it were a little more kid-friendly. “I opted for wainscoting on the lower half of the walls to protect the wallpaper from sticky fingers,” she says.

It has been revealed that this is one of two generously sized guest bedroom suites, so friends and family will never feel short-changed when it’s time to hit the hay. It also has some of the most intriguing decorative details in the entire house. “The gingham four-poster bed is the star of the room, and I love the playful contrast between its bold check and the floral Roman shades,” she claims. The wall accents are equally as enviable. “The framed Hermès scarf is another longtime favorite, which I sourced at Round Top over a decade ago, before Round Top was cool!”.

Hoffman took a light-touch approach to her daughter’s room, knowing that the seven-year-old would eventually want to put her own stylistic signature on it. “I wanted to create a room that felt charming and playful without being overly childish, with pieces she could continue to enjoy as she grows,” she notes. Beyond painting the walls a pretty blush pink, the only real change here was adding custom Roman shades, which give the room a more tailored, finished feel.

Recent findings suggest that this primary bathroom saw a full gut renovation to bring it up to the standards of modern living. Along with adding his-and-hers sinks and a freestanding tub, Hoffman took the opportunity to correct an architectural eyesore: the two mismatched windows that created irritating asymmetry. “We ultimately replaced both windows, incorporating diamond-pattern mullions in the upper third to complement the home’s Tudor architecture,” she adds. “It was a significant expense, but it gave us greater flexibility with the layout and brought a sense of continuity to the room.”.

This guest room is an homage to the family’s life in London, as much of the decor came from their former home across the pond. The art, too, was sourced from a local printmaker whose studio was down the street in the family’s old neighborhood. Any fresh additions here were smaller and strategic. “The Schumacher floral fabric on the curtains and pillows became the thread that tied everything together, bringing color, pattern, and a sense of cohesion to the room,” Hoffman claims.

The kids’ bathroom was reworked with total flexibility in mind. “With a son and a daughter sharing the space, I wanted a palette that felt playful and fresh without leaning either too feminine or masculine,” Hoffman notes. While the existing floor tile stayed, she added a custom double vanity so both kids can brush their teeth at the same time, as well as painted beadboard wainscoting to extend the country-home atmosphere into the washroom.

Industry observers note that kaitlyn Hoffman is the founder of Studio Proper, a boutique residential interior design firm located in Denver, Colorado. She’s a British citizen and lifelong Anglophile whose signature style was honed over nearly a decade living in London. Her design sensibility takes inspiration from traditional English interiors but adds a modern, practical twist.

Wood, Glass, Porcelain, and Beyond: Jewelry’s Alternative Material Crush

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (696 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
  • Industry observers note that one of the greatest things about the best kinds of jewelry is that it has no limits.
  • On the runways recently, we’ve seen Chanel and Dries Van Noten toy with glass necklaces, Margiela play with porcelain (in the form of an ASMR-worthy dress that was an undercover nod to the house’s famous ’90s vest made of the material) as well as multilayered tidbits in standout pieces like Celine’s charm necklaces.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Industry observers note that one of the greatest things about the best kinds of jewelry is that it has no limits. Unlike clothing, it can pretty much be made out of anything, so long as it’s durable. Glass, in jewelry, dates as far back as around 3500 BCE in ancient Mesopotamia and Egypt, via beads and carvings. Yet all these years later, designers are revisiting the humble material, along with wood, porcelain, and beyond. It makes sense: We’re definitely in an era of experimental jewelry, and materials that push beyond the typical precious metals and gemstones allow for bolder shapes and silhouettes, with major impact. Enter: wooden pendants, glass rings, and porcelain chains.

On the runways recently, we’ve seen Chanel and Dries Van Noten toy with glass necklaces, Margiela play with porcelain (in the form of an ASMR-worthy dress that was an undercover nod to the house’s famous ’90s vest made of the material) as well as multilayered tidbits in standout pieces like Celine’s charm necklaces.

Likewise, fine jewelers are integrating various materials into their work. Marla Aaron, for instance, reimagined her Lock connector pendant in an official collaboration with Nymphenburg porcelain. Marie Lichtenberg makes beautiful dice pendants rendered in black ebony and diamonds. Anna Maccieri Rossi recently released an entire collection dedicated to wood, including chunky necklaces and carved bangles set with gemstones. “I love wood because it is a living material, warm and natural,” she said of the collection. “This material offers me the chance to dream and work on a large scale, with a bolder approach.”.

In a recent development, the cost of gold rapidly ascended in 2025, reaching an all-time nominal record high of $5,589.38 per troy ounce in January 2026. Driven by historic market shifts and a broader surge in precious metal prices, this sharp economic rise has dramatically reshaped how fashion insiders, collectors, and everyday jewelry lovers approach their collections. As traditional solid gold pieces become increasingly rare financial splurges, buyers are actively diversifying their wardrobes with creative, tactile alternatives. In addition to gravitating toward vintage sterling silver and archival heirlooms, jewelry aficionados are now getting their fix with these alternative materials—ranging from hand-carved wood and delicate hand-blown glass to sculptural porcelain and unconventional metals.

Some designers, too, are looking to build and reinvent the legacy of those who came before them. “I think when most people hear ‘glass jewelry,’ a pretty specific image comes to mind,” Colin Keane Lynch of Keane New York tells ELLE. “I’m interested in building on that history while exploring some of the less familiar possibilities.” Lynch, who has devoted his life to working with glass, designs sculptural glass petal rings and sinuous cuffs, all made to order. “Another thing I love about glass is its ability to take on the appearance of so many different materials through explorations of form, texture, and color. It also allows me to create things that might be difficult or even impossible to achieve in other materials.”.

In a recent development, much like the language and energy of crystals and gemstones, others are interested in these materials because of what they represent. Take Thatch, for instance. Founded by Amy Goin and Laura Laing, the brand sells huge wooden heart pendants as well as fish-shaped wooden bangles and charms. “We feel that wood holds energy the same way gemstones do,” indicates Goin. “A different kind of energy. Something quieter and more grounded. It’s soulful and raw. We love the bohemian beauty of wood, paired with a touch of gold and sparkle.”.

For today’s designers, the most precious thing about jewelry is the possibility.

Anna Maccieri Rossi Ora Wood Sunrise Ring with Pink Sapphire.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Above: To celebrate Bulgari’s latest collection and boutique, guests roamed the grounds of a waterfront Palm Beach estate, designed by architect Addison Mizner.

In a recent development, few people shaped the look of South Florida as much as architect Addison Mizner. A pioneer of Spanish Colonial Revival architecture, his Mediterranean style quickly took Palm Beach by storm in the 1920s, as he designed and built more than 50 Florida mansions and villas. And his impact still lingers, as, on Wednesday night, stars like Venus Williams and Chanel Iman spent their evening seated under the tennis pavilion at one of Mizner’s famed waterfront Palm Beach estates.

The crowd was there to celebrate a far newer building in the neighborhood: Bulgari’s Palm Beach boutique, which opened earlier this week. In honor of the store’s debut, the brand brought its newest high jewelry collection, Eclettica, to the United States for the first time.

“Palm Beach embodies a distinctive spirit of effortless sophistication,” mentioned Bulgari CEO Laura Burdese.

Located in a heritage building in Palm Beach’s shopping district, the boutique is modeled after a traditional Italian piazza. Anchored by four travertine columns, the open space encourages clients to move through the maison’s most famous collections. Venini’s classic Serpenti chandelier, made of Murano glass and seen in Bvlgari boutiques worldwide, serves as a focal point in a shape reminiscent of the brand’s many symbolic snakes.

It has been revealed that elsewhere in the store, decorative panels by Milan-based Pictalab depict Floridian ocean and beach views, grounding the Italian maison in its surrounding landscape. Among the art is the Eclettica collection, which borrows its name from eclecticism and stays true to its moniker: mixing inspirations from painting, sculpture, and architecture, translating them into bold, colorful pieces.

It’s a fitting style for Palm Beach, where Mizner’s vibrant Mediterranean and Spanish-influenced designs borrow inspiration from entire eras and regions, giving the area its everlasting mix-master flair.

“We are delighted to bring Eclettica to this extraordinary destination,” Burdese said, “where its bold artistic vision and exceptional craftsmanship find a natural resonance with the city’s vibrant character.”.

Industry observers note that if the late, great, legendary fashion editor Diana Vreeland were still alive, I believe she would incorporate a question like, “Why don’t you replace your ring stacks with statement gloves?” into her famous “Why don’t you” column, where she rhetorically mused on ridiculous and often opulent situations. A good glove is a winter staple, yes. But lately, fashion has been having a love affair with embellished, stylized gloves. We’ve now seen the opera glove in all of its forms. But what about gloves bedecked in crystal cuffs, neon hues, faux fur effects, and beyond? They’ve already arrived, on the runways and at retailers.

Sources indicate that consider Givenchy’s leather wonders, which come in ballooning silhouettes that envelop the hands and wrists. Or Prada’s spring/summer 2026 silky satin opera gloves in shades of pale yellow or olive green. With delicate ruching throughout, the formal opera glove gets an ironic, modern, slouched, and louche makeover. Elsewhere, Khaite has shown the power of an opera-length glove in python. Clearly, texture is an embellishment all its own in these kinds of extreme examples.

In a recent development, in some cases, the gloves become the jewelry. In others, jewelry further accents the statement glove, like for Mugler’s fall/winter 2026 show in which models wore kelly green and royal purple scrunched leather gloves up to their elbows, sometimes styled with a big chunky bracelet over top. Elsewhere, some gloves were mismatched: vivid yellow on one hand and brilliant blue on the other. The brand called it a fresh take on power dressing, which melded codes of the 1980s, 1940s, and 17th-century aristocratic court coats. “Ultimately, this show intends to acknowledge that self-empowerment is the most potent antidote of clarity to the oppressive forces and grey political climate that surrounds us at this very moment,” Mugler creative director Castro Freitas was quoted in the show notes, “and most of all, it’s a manifesto of the highest power that we should never forget to reclaim: FREEDOM.”.

It has been revealed that most of all, the statement glove dresses up any neutral wool coat or adds an extra layer of over-the-top theatrics to a statement coat. When in doubt, you could also simply opt for a colorful glove, which the runways have loved in droves lately. Take, for example, Valentino, which has been pumping out short and statement-making silky gloves in shades of ’80s neon pink or dreamy cobalt blue.

Industry observers note that sometimes, all you need is a change of silhouette, too. At Chanel, the fingerless glove has long been a staple, and it’s now become a favorite of superfan clients during street style moments between shows. Elsewhere, the fingerless glove has forever been a celeb favorite, especially when it comes to style legends like Madonna.

“We’ve got every color under the rainbow of gloves and/or a sheer opera-length glove that is in either a matching color or an opposite color of whatever the look is,” Madonna’s stylist Rita Melssen told ELLE in August 2026.

One thing is clear: Statement gloves are the newly introduced power accessory, equal parts practical, theatrical, and impossible to ignore.

Breaking: Frog Closures Are the Unexpected Detail Defining Fall Jackets

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (461 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are plenty of ways to make a statement with your outerwear, from an oversize silhouette to a high collar or bold color.
  • Sources indicate that in particular, frog fastenings are having a resurgence, bringing a fanciful finishing touch to everything from minimalist wool peacoats to tailored military-inspired jackets.
  • While they may seem upcoming for the season, frog-fastener jackets have a history that spans centuries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are plenty of ways to make a statement with your outerwear, from an oversize silhouette to a high collar or bold color. But this fall, designers are turning their attention to a smaller detail: the fastening. Jackets featuring decorative knots, elaborate loops, and ornate toggles have emerged as one of the season’s biggest outerwear trends, offering an alternative to standard buttons and zippers.

Sources indicate that in particular, frog fastenings are having a resurgence, bringing a fanciful finishing touch to everything from minimalist wool peacoats to tailored military-inspired jackets. Typically constructed from fabric or braided cord, the fasteners consist of a knotted button and a loop. Originally designed to secure garments, the closures have evolved into a more ornamental role with intricate shapes and floral-like designs.

While they may seem upcoming for the season, frog-fastener jackets have a history that spans centuries. In Chinese dress, knotted closures known as pankou have long appeared on garments such as the qipao and tangzhuang. By the 18th and 19th centuries, frogging had also become a feature of European military uniforms, worn by cavalry regiments whose fitted jackets were adorned with braided cords.

It has been revealed that fashion has revisited the detail since then. Oscar de la Renta incorporated frog fastenings into his designs in the 1990s, while Valentino explored versions for its fall 2015 couture collection. More recently, for fall 2026, designers reinterpreted knotted closures: At Kallmeyer, black toggles punctuated a gilded jacquard jacket, while Kim Shui incorporated the detail into fur-trimmed blazers and opera jackets. Meanwhile, labels like Khaite and Ann Demeulemeester embraced military-inspired looks featuring ornamental braiding and embellished fronts.

Today’s store-rack versions range from collarless blazers with understated knots to dramatic outerwear designs featuring detailed cording. Brands like Róhe have introduced contemporary takes on frogging, while Hong Kong–based fashion label Sau Lee has reimagined traditional Tang-style jackets with modern silhouettes.

Rather than reinventing jackets entirely, designers are proving that something as minuscule as a fastening can make a familiar silhouette feel new again for the season. Ahead, shop our favorite takes on the look.

On the Couch: Tina Barney

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (822 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 1974, Tina Barney moved from New York City to Sun Valley, Idaho, a quiet, picturesque ski hamlet set within the Rocky Mountains.
  • The daughter of 1940s fashion model Lillian Fox and granddaughter of the founder of Lehman Brothers, Barney is known for documenting high society with a sharp eye, photographing affluent Americans, European aristocrats, and lavish spaces.
  • In honor of her book’s release, Barney took our On the Couch survey, sharing a few of her biggest influences and inspirations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 1974, Tina Barney moved from New York City to Sun Valley, Idaho, a quiet, picturesque ski hamlet set within the Rocky Mountains. It was there, while taking an art school class on great American photographers, that she began shooting photographs herself. In the five-plus decades that followed, Barney became a legendary American photographer in her own right, with works entering the permanent collections of museums like the Whitney, the Museum of Modern Art, and the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.

The daughter of 1940s fashion model Lillian Fox and granddaughter of the founder of Lehman Brothers, Barney is known for documenting high society with a sharp eye, photographing affluent Americans, European aristocrats, and lavish spaces. She also captured what they wore—and shot for fashion magazines and major designers like Gucci and Bottega Veneta. Barney’s relationship with style, stemming from her mother’s work with fashion photographers like Horst P. Horst and George Hoyningen-Huene, is the subject of her new book Tina Barney: Fashion, out now.

In honor of her book’s release, Barney took our On the Couch survey, sharing a few of her biggest influences and inspirations.

According to recent reports, greatest Influences: I made a film on Jan Groover. I made a film on Horst P. Horst. And you can see the photos he took of my mom in the newly introduced book.

Favorite Sofa: My couch has been in this house for decades, and I am probably getting a upcoming one because this one's falling apart. But it is in the right place with the right light. I can watch TV; I can read; I can draw; I can do anything I want from this place. And it's comfortable.

Most beloved buildings: I did a whole book on the Noguchi Museum, a portrait of Isamu Noguchi’s building, in a way, and of his sculpture.

According to recent reports, destination Museum: The Musée d’Orsay. It’s the way the paintings are hung that really interests me. There are artworks placed within little cubicles, and then, of course, there are the most well-known paintings that are just so easy to keep looking at. So the Musée d'Orsay first, followed by almost any other museum in Paris.

Go-to galleries: It depends on the artist that is showing. In New York, I go out to look at galleries every month with a friend. We’ll see what the new highlights are, and I always try to learn from what I see.

In a recent development, favorite Artist: I don't like to name names because there are no favorites. But I just saw a Brice Marden show at Gagosian that was tops.

According to recent reports, favorite getaway: I travel as little as possible right now. I live in Rhode Island part-time, more so than in New York. Here it is quiet.

Best Shop for Gifts: Well, I love agnès b. She’s very supportive of photographers, so that’s how I came to know her, and I still visit her shop in New York.

Best Host/Hostess Gift: A favorite book.

It has been revealed that style Icons: I don't think of buzzwords like that. But, my mother for sure. Her style was led by her sense of humor, and by her own personality. In those days, you weren't thinking about the fashion designers and who was in and who was out. And so the clothes had much more character to them.

Industry observers note that my mother brought me to an Yves Saint Laurent fashion show in Paris when I was about 16, which I remember very well. It was the first show that Yves Saint Laurent ever had on his own. We also saw the designer Guy Laroche; we went in after the show and my mother had a suit made for her, so they measured her. And that was a pretty fantastic experience.

Fashion Designers: I have a picture of me from about when I was age 14 and I'm wearing a suit that looks like a Chanel. And because they were starting to copy her at that point, you could get a viable suit for someone 14 or 16 years old that looked like a Chanel. I love that the style of Chanel has existed for so long, and has not changed that much.

It has been revealed that required Reading: Katie Kitamura. Also, Judith Freeman, my favorite author, who I know is working on a upcoming novel.

Cocktail of Choice: I don’t drink; I never have. I’m like a monk.

Favorite Restaurant: The Olympia Tea Room in Watch Hill, Rhode Island.

Favorite Jeweler: Elsa Peretti.

#54677. Latest Update: Which Ultra-Processed Foods Are the Worst for You? A Dietitian Breaks It Down

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2159 w)
