📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

As a chronic nail biter (gross, I know), I’ve tried just about every type of manicure out there in an attempt to heal my nails and kick my habit. From acrylics and tips to builder gel and dip powder, nothing has ever worked for me. But one simple option has never let me down: press-ons. They provide a natural-looking manicure without damaging your nails, take just minutes to apply, and can be done from the comfort of your own home. There’s no drying, intense filing, or pricey appointments required. What’s not to love?

It has been revealed that recently, I fell down a glue-filled rabbit hole in search of the best press-on nails out there. Every week, I’d apply a new set in the name of research, meticulously assessing each for quality, durability, and longevity. I have very small nail beds, so finding a size, shape, and length that fit my fingertips was essential. After about a year of testing (and an absurd amount of nail glue), there was a clear winner: Glamnetic.

Industry observers note that we praised the product last year, and that praise still holds true. The application is not only simple, but I actually find it quite therapeutic. I start by pushing back my cuticles with the included wooden stick and filing the entire surface of the nails, not just the edges. Doing this helps the press-ons adhere better and last longer. Next, I match each of my fingers to the best-fitting press-on. Finally, I remove any oils from my nails using the alcohol pad, and glue on the set. I start with my pinkies and move toward my thumbs, placing a dot of glue at the base of each press-on and holding it down for about 30 to 45 seconds. Before I know it, I’m left with a perfect manicure that’s affordable, natural-looking, and long-lasting.

Sources indicate that while it’s always fun to experiment with different shapes and lengths, my personal favorite is the brand’s “Short Oval” collection. For under $20, each set comes with 30 nails in varying sizes, and all of the above materials. They are incredibly durable without looking or feeling thick, and each set lasts about two weeks.

Whether you prefer a milky pink shade like Strawberry Icing or a more festive set like Snowfall, Glamnetic is known for its impressive designs. From magnetic cat-eye polish to 3-D chrome appliqués, there’s a set for every style, season, and mood. For a nail biter who has destroyed just about every expensive manicure imaginable, finding a budget-friendly option that can actually keep up with me feels like a small miracle.

An intimate holiday dinner with Chanel to celebrate its watches and fine jewelry.

Recent findings suggest that on an unseasonably warm Tuesday night in New York, the French fashion house hosted ambassadors, friends, and more at Daniel Humm’s new, already hard-to-reserve restaurant, HUMM. As she got ready for her outing, the 25-year-old was as relaxed as ever. In a downtown hotel room, a scene unfolded that any 20-something woman would recognize: “Wide Open Spaces” by The Chicks played on a speaker (a song Rubin calls her “Annie anthem”), a light girl dinner of French fries and soda splayed across a table, and a friend on hand for moral support.

In a recent development, rubin, an Upper West Side native herself, knows that for a Manhattan night on the town, sometimes less is more. The actress opted for a black tweed jacket—in true Gabrielle Chanel fashion—from look 40 of the Métiers d’art 2026 collection. Paired with a simple white tank and perfectly fitting Levi’s, “it’s my ideal dinner look,” she says.

In terms of accessories, Rubin wore a Chanel Première Ribbon watch, with diamonds elegantly placed around the face. “A beautiful gift,” she says, “and also something you’ll have forever, which is sort of the cornerstone of why I love Chanel jewelry so much, as it’s pieces you’ll know and love, and hopefully, give to someone someday.”.

In a recent development, despite not having her ears pierced, Rubin’s accessories game remains strong. The simplicity of Rubin’s outfit allowed for her jewels to truly shine as she finished off her look with stacked Chanel Fine Jewelry Coco Crush ear cuffs and rings in 18K white gold and diamonds. For glam, makeup artist Shayna Goldberg kept things natural and dewy, starting with a seamless base of Chanel Beauty Les Beiges Healthy Glow Foundation, topped off with the Les Beiges Healthy Glow Natural Eyeshadow Palette and Les Beiges Mascara. The finishing touch? Rouge Coco Longwear Satin Lipstick in 124 Marie and Le Crayon Lèvres Precision Lip-Defining Pencil in Nude Brun.

Below, Rubin reflects on her busy year, plots her holiday gifting list—Chanel included, of course—and reveals who she’d most like to guest star on season 2 of Sterling Point. Someone get Julia Roberts on the phone, stat!

It has been revealed that I’m in a really lovely structured jacket, with this high kind of collar, and really beautiful buttons. They’re just so ornate and detailed. So, I’m really glad that I’m getting to explore that side of jewelry. And then, I love a watch, and I love rings. Those are sort of my staples, my favorites.

Sources indicate that it almost feels too late for me. I did it when I was a kid. And they closed up immediately, because I played soccer, and I just wasn’t committed. Now we’re just rocking with it, and it almost feels like, “Okay, this is just where we're at, and where we're staying.” But because Chanel makes such wonderful clip-ons, I get the opportunity to wear lovely earrings now.

Oh, my God. All of them. So many of them. Some of the cuffs I’m wearing tonight, honestly, luckily, they don’t need me to have my ears pierced for them, but if I had to, I would.

According to recent reports, something that’s comfortable, that feels like a part of you, and a part of your outfit. Something where you feel like yourself, it’s an extension of you.

There is this Coco Crush ring that I have now, very, very luckily. It’s on one side, just metal. And then, on the other side, it’s diamonds. And it’s just shiny and beautiful, and lovely, and it feels both, really simple and casual, and also, a party in the back.

Sources indicate that that’s a great question. I think a watch is an incredible gift. I’ve had the pleasure of wearing a Chanel watch tonight, and on the show I’m on. It feels just like an incredible staple that, of course, also has utility, and it’s really classic and useful, and a beautiful gift.

It’s just so wild. It’s very surreal. So that's really the ultimate goal. I just feel unbelievably fortunate to be in the position to keep working. So it's pretty wonderful. It's solely wonderful, yeah. I’m just going to choose to keep enjoying it, and sharing it with the people I love.

Always Sex in the City, of course. I watch a lot of movies. I recently saw Wild Horse Nine. I think, for fall and winter, going to the theater is the best activity. It’s my favorite thing to do in the world, but especially as it’s getting colder, it’s just an incredibly cozy, wonderful time to go do that kind of thing. I’ve been in the theater almost every single day. Catch me at any AMC or Film Forum.

I’m obsessed with Alison Oliver. Maybe we could discover another sister, and it’s a biological sister, and it’s Annie’s sister. I’m just desperate to work with so many actors. So I’m thinking of Julia Roberts, Viola Davis. I’m naming all my favorite actors in the world. Oh, my God. Susannah Perkins. I just did God of the Woods with them. They’re fantastic. I would do anything to work with them again.

According to recent reports, get ready for more laughing and crying. Season two is still being figured out, so there's so much I don't even know, but I will say I think we're going to only become more intimately close with these characters, and know them more deeply.

Latest Update: Dreaming of Buying a Home Abroad? These 10 Countries Make It Shockingly Simple

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1220 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over the last few years, many Americans have daydreamed about life abroad.
  • In a recent development, certain countries, like Australia, Canada, and Latest Zealand, have bans on foreign buyers.
  • Sources indicate that choosing the right location can make moving abroad much less intimidating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the last few years, many Americans have daydreamed about life abroad. Moving internationally can often feel like a pipe dream, but with the right planning, it’s possible. However, lengthy visa processes, daunting language barriers, and a difficult-to-navigate legal system can make the dream feel more like a nightmare.

In a recent development, certain countries, like Australia, Canada, and Latest Zealand, have bans on foreign buyers. Others, like Thailand, Cuba, and Vietnam, don’t allow outsiders to own property at all. On the other end of the spectrum are countries actively trying to attract foreign buyers, offering enviable incentives like affordable home prices, a smoother customs process, and an easier-to-navigate work-visa approval process.

Sources indicate that choosing the right location can make moving abroad much less intimidating. Ahead, we’re breaking down the ten best countries for Americans looking to buy property abroad. Whether you’re dreaming of relocating or searching for your perfect vacation home, these countries make buying as easy as possible and offer gorgeous landscapes too.

According to recent reports, if you’ve ever dreamed of living among medieval architecture and rolling mountain ranges, Georgia might be the key to unlocking your fantasy. A bridge between Eastern Europe and Western Asia, the transcontinental country borders Russia, Turkey, Armenia, and the Black Sea, offering both subtropical and high-altitude climates. Thankfully, the real estate landscape is much less complex, with few legal or bureaucratic hurdles for American buyers, no residency or visa required (for up to a year), and remarkably fast processing times. In fact, the only major restriction in the Georgia market is that foreigners cannot purchase or own agricultural land, a nod to the importance of the local, small-scale farming cultures peppered across the country’s regions.

Recent findings suggest that uruguay’s buying process could not be more straightforward. South America’s second-smallest sovereign country requires no citizenship, visa, or prior approvals. Under Uruguayan law, foreign buyers are given the same rights as citizens and enjoy the benefits of free capital flow. Locals are just as, if not more, tourist-friendly. The country is known for its hospitality, laid-back café culture, and stunning coastal landscapes.

Sources indicate that instead of retiring to Florida, consider this balmy, beautiful Caribbean country—just a four-hour direct flight from the Newly introduced York area. Like everything else on the island, the real estate laws are relatively relaxed, making buying a house easy-breezy; and you can buy and own property without obtaining residency status or special permissions, as is the case in many other Caribbean islands. “Foreigners can own property outright in the Dominican Republic, with legal protections for foreign investors,” states Mauricio Umansky, CEO and founder of The Agency. One key consideration is financing: You can certainly get a mortgage in the DR, but it may not be quite as cushy as what you can get in the U.S.—so pay cash if possible.

Recent findings suggest that great news if you’ve been wanting a more provincial life: Americans face zero restrictions when buying homes in France. The open market allows for statesiders to buy houses, apartments, or plots of land in the city, countryside, and coastal towns in person or remotely without needing citizenship, residency, or even a local visa. However, a purchase does not grant residency, so if you’re hoping to make France your permanent home, you’ll want to apply for a separate long-stay visa and note the Schengen 90-out-of-180-day rule. While buying may be simple, the finances are anything but. Closing fees, including notary fees, typically add seven to ten percent to your purchase. Mortgage rates are also incredibly hard to secure for U.S.-based buyers, thanks to strict debt-to-income caps and FATCA compliance. To simplify the process, many buyers opt to put 20 percent to 40 percent down in cash.

Perhaps the most American-friendly market, Panama boasts a large English-speaking market, virtually no restrictions on foreign property ownership, and uses the U.S. dollar as legal tender in a vastly affordable market. The Central American nation also offers residency programs like the Friendly Nations Visa, clearing the way legally for residency by investment. In addition to an efficient legal system and reliable market, Panama boasts breathtaking beaches, lush rainforests, and exceptional wildlife.

Industry observers note that if you’re hoping for a home in the coffee valleys of Colombia, you’ll need to hire a real estate lawyer before you start scouting for mountain chalets, coffee triangle treehouses, and rainforest retreats. The Caribbean country opts out of standardized agent licensing systems, making legal aid essential to verify title and freedom certificates. While citizenship isn’t required, you will need to secure a tourist visa and Colombian Tax ID to complete your purchase and register for property taxes.

The buying process in Greece is lengthy, though it is streamlined, with a clear checklist for American buyers to find success in the market. Hiring a local lawyer or notary is a great first step after scouting properties. Not only are they familiar with title checks and contracts, but they can also navigate the intricacies that come with buying in designated border areas or near military zones, which require special clearance for non–EU buyers. While the most popular areas for American buyers, like Athens and Crete, don’t come with heavy legal intricacies, buying any property in Greece will mean securing a Greek Tax Number—a small price to pay for cities with such rich histories and breathtaking seaside views.

Sources indicate that the people in this popular Western European coastal country are famously friendly and inviting, and that extends to real estate. According to Samira Easton, a certified international property specialist with Premier Sotheby’s International Realty, Portugal offers a Golden Visa Program, which makes it simple to buy property and gain residency; clear real estate laws; and a well-established network of English-speaking real estate agents, lawyers, and notaries to help you during the process.

According to recent reports, belize is home to one of the most vibrant, tourist-friendly cultures in Central America, mixing Mayan, Hispanic, Asian, and Creole cultures in its dense rainforests and rolling low plains. Buying here is as easy as it can get, as outright ownership applies to foreigners, and a British-inspired legal system abolishes language barriers and makes contracts easier to understand. Even more, there is no capital gains tax in Belize, and property taxes trend low. The country also boasts vibrant marine life and is home to the world’s second-largest barrier reef.

Spain may have ended its investor visa program in 2025, but the real estate market is still remarkably easy for Americans to navigate. The country presently imposes no restrictions on foreign or nonresident property ownership, but there are a few things you’ll need to procure before you buy, like a Foreigner Identification Number, which is mandatory for taxes. Despite the minor hurdles, the market is booming both on the ground and online. “There are also numerous online resources and property portals available, so it’s easy to find listings and information,” Easton indicates. This is a boon for those who aren’t able to make the trip over to Europe to house shop in person.Note that buying property does not grant you residency or bypass the country’s 90-day Schengen limit. If you’re hoping to turn your Spanish holiday into your everyday, you’ll have to apply for a separate visa.

Above: Listed for $75 million, the Hillandale estate sits on 268 acres in Stamford, Connecticut.

In a recent development, HBO’s The Gilded Age is back for a fourth season, once again bringing viewers into the lavish homes where the Russell and van Rhijn families’ dramas unfold. Filmed at some of the era’s most impressive estates, the series serves up grand ballrooms, château-style manors, and sumptuous drapery in abundance. It’s enough to stir up a little real estate envy. Fortunately, three extraordinary Gilded Age homes are currently on the market, offering the chance to live out that fantasy in real life. Take a peek inside below.

Industry observers note that dating to the turn of the century, this lavish European-style estate—known as Hillandale—once belonged to the Sulzberger family, owners of The Upcoming York Times. Located along the Connecticut border with New York, the star of the 268-acre compound is an eight-bedroom mansion designed by architecture firm Hunt & Hunt that spans more than 15,000 square feet. Featuring elaborate millwork, moldings, plasterwork, and stained glass, the manor features plenty of amenities. Olympic-sized indoor pool? Check. Elevator? There are two. Grounds? They include formal gardens, four guest houses, a private lake, and even a hedge maze. The opulent spread is listed with Leslie McElwreath of Sotheby’s International Realty.

Sources indicate that an Anglo-Italianate brownstone in Latest York’s Chelsea Historic District, the Van Ness House was built in the mid-19th century and was later enlarged to its present 7,800-square-foot size. Revamped by ELLE Decor A-List designer Miles Redd, the seven-level landmark pays homage to its elegant roots, with preserved plaster moldings, custom millwork, elegant wallcoverings, and heated oak floors in a retro chevron pattern. In the back, a landscaped private garden is paved in limestone and dotted with linden trees that turn golden in the fall. Atop the five-bedroom townhouse, which is listed with Nick Gavin and Amber Gregory of Compass, is a rooftop garden with views of Saint Peter’s Church.

According to recent reports, spanning 14,100 square feet, this Beaux-Arts mansion right off Fifth Avenue was constructed in 1902 by architect James R. Turner and William G. Killian. Its interiors, meanwhile, are by John Russell Pope, the genius behind the Jefferson Memorial and the National Gallery of Art. Clad in a medley of brick, limestone, and marble, the eight-bedroom house has retained its stately proportions throughout the years, including a formal dining room lined in carved wood panels. Also inside are a trio of staircases, an elevator servicing six of the seven floors, and two rooftop terraces. It’s listed for $35 million with Brian Meier and Amanda Barba of Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices.

Geoffrey Montes is an associate editor at ELLE Decor with a serious love for all things real estate and design. Before that, he worked at Architectural Digest, Galerie, and Preservation magazines, covering everything from jaw-dropping listings to world-famous architects and design events like Salone del Mobile and Homo Faber.

Yesterday afternoon, the Oscar winner revealed to the world that she had given birth to her little one when she stepped out for a stroll in Upcoming York City, smiling widely as she carried her newborn—a daughter—swaddled to her chest in a brown velvet baby carrier.

The only part of Hathaway’s youngest that was visible was her head, snuggled in a plum-colored beanie decorated with a tiny pink pom-pom, which peeked out from the top of the carrier.

In these first public photos with her newborn, Hathaway sported not only a substantial grin, but also a luxury gray overcoat from Brunello Cucinelli, which she layered over white sweats and a lavender knit sweater. She completed the cozy fit with brown suede Rothy’s clogs and a black baseball cap.

According to TMZ, who first broke the photos, the Verity star was seen walking around with a friend, who even stopped to capture snaps of Hathaway with her newborn.

The Devil Wears Prada 2 star and her husband, Adam Schulman, are also parents to sons Jonathan and Jack, who were born in 2016 and 2019, respectively. Hathaway has yet to reveal when exactly she gave birth to their third child, or the name of their daughter, but the sex was revealed in a congratulatory Instagram Story by her costume designer, Molly Rogers.

After months of witnessing Hathaway’s incredible maternity style as she promoted her many projects of the year, we’re ready to be inspired by her mom fashion.

First, there’s determining the budget; then it’s figuring out whether to get them something practical, fun, edible, or just plain silly. I even gave them to a coworker whose hands were chronically cold in the office, and she used them all year long!”.

Every group has a crafty team member, which makes this LEGO set a good gift to give. They can build it at work during their lunch break and display it on their desk. Best of all, they don’t have to worry about their florals or greenery dying when they come back from the holiday break.

Sources indicate that the portable lunch box options for adults aren’t nearly as cute as the ones for kids, so we went on the hunt for a nice one and found this pick from Kate Spade New York. In a recent development, we can't get enough of these cheeky cocktail napkins with the ingredients for a perfect Caesar salad. The coworker who's always shaking up a salad bowl around lunchtime will get a kick out of this.

The personality hire is a key role in any office dynamic. Say thank you to the person who keeps things fun with this chic game box, complete with playing cards, dice, and a classy velvet lining.

Industry observers note that putting together the staff holiday party is no easy task. Thank the coworker responsible for this finishing touch for the office Christmas tree: a set of scented tree stems. They complete the festive atmosphere by bringing the scent of fir and spruce to the office.

This calming bonsai plant does well in low-light, so it's great for office environments. Brighten up their desk and give them something to look forward to when they come in each morning. You can even name it for an extra personal touch.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Singing Bird on a Clock and Bird on a Rock brooch, 800-843-3269.
  • In a recent development, how does a yellow cockatoo flitting near an open window in Guadeloupe end up a jewelry icon?
  • How to keep reaching newly introduced heights?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Above: Tiffany & Co. Singing Bird on a Clock and Bird on a Rock brooch, 800-843-3269.

In a recent development, how does a yellow cockatoo flitting near an open window in Guadeloupe end up a jewelry icon? That bird knew what it was doing when it perched outside the home of Jean Schlumberger, one of Tiffany & Co’s best-known jewelry designers. Nature was always the apple of Schlumberger’s eye, and in his vision that bird would become a diamond-studded feathered friend nestled in lapis lazuli and pinned on Bunny Mellon’s beret (he would go on to make for her a full, whimsical bestiary. Theirs was a partnership of hundreds of jelly fish, camels, and seahorses, plus the beloved fruit and flowers inspired by Mellon’s own garden).

That was 1965. How to keep reaching newly introduced heights? A partnership between Tiffany & Co. and the Musée des Arts Décoratifs (MAD) in Paris offers inspiration: An archive of thousands of Schlumberger’s sketches, now being restored and digitized, reveal a mind constantly at work and a vision without boundaries. And so it continues, in spessartine and chrysoprase, in rubellites and mother-of-pearl, and turquoise. The next reincarnation of the bird, though, might be one of the most exciting horological spectacles of the year: a glimmering, singing automata atop a burst of sun, a singing gold and titanium bird on a clock. Though, we must note, it does not play music: instead, it tweets. Look, and listen.

This story originally appeared in the November 2026 issue of ELLE Decor.

Editor-in-Chief Stellene Volandes is a jewelry expert, and the author of Jeweler: Masters and Mavericks of Modern Design (Rizzoli).

Industry News: Harry Styles-Approved Designer Macy Grimshaw Just Won the 2026 H&M Design Award

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (540 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Earlier this year, Macy Grimshaw presented her graduate collection from Central Saint Martins at London Fashion Week, styled by Harry Lambert, the mind behind the wardrobes of Emma Corrin, Alexander Skarsgård, and Harry Styles.
  • At the presentation on Wednesday afternoon in London, Grimshaw was chosen among seven other finalists from top design universities across the globe: Chico Yu, Ennis Finnerty Mackay, Evelina Kryvopust, Fantin Delattre Pirenne, Jessica Lin, Macy Grimshaw, Yichun Liu, and Yvonne Schichtel.
  • “She left me with desire and intrigue to see how she can actually develop the work,” mentioned Beka Gvishiani, founder of Style Not Com, who joined H&M’s creative advisor Ann-Sofie Johansson, model Paloma Elsesser, and designer Ib Kamara on the jury.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Earlier this year, Macy Grimshaw presented her graduate collection from Central Saint Martins at London Fashion Week, styled by Harry Lambert, the mind behind the wardrobes of Emma Corrin, Alexander Skarsgård, and Harry Styles. Since then, the 25-year-old designer has continued to rise, dressing the likes of Anya Taylor-Joy, Simone Ashley, and several of Lambert’s clients—Corrin and Styles among them—in her semi-surrealist separates and top-notch leatherwork. Now, Grimshaw has a major accolade to cap off her standout year: the 2026 H&M Design Award.

At the presentation on Wednesday afternoon in London, Grimshaw was chosen among seven other finalists from top design universities across the globe: Chico Yu, Ennis Finnerty Mackay, Evelina Kryvopust, Fantin Delattre Pirenne, Jessica Lin, Macy Grimshaw, Yichun Liu, and Yvonne Schichtel. Grimshaw will receive a €150,000 ($164,655) endowment, a yearlong mentorship, and will have her collection produced and sold in selected H&M stores worldwide and online in October 2027. Each finalist was awarded a €10,000 ($10,980) endowment.

“She left me with desire and intrigue to see how she can actually develop the work,” mentioned Beka Gvishiani, founder of Style Not Com, who joined H&M’s creative advisor Ann-Sofie Johansson, model Paloma Elsesser, and designer Ib Kamara on the jury. “For the moment, it’s very much the artist’s work,” he continued. “But she has ideas about how to make it wearable for daywear, because some of the pieces are great for an event or a performance.”.

Gvishiani highlights the collection’s more experimental pieces, like a rusted, laser-cut mesh minidress ornamented with padlocks or a terracotta-hued molded bustier scattered with discarded cigarette butts. The scenography of the latter was inspired, naturally, by the brick wall where CSM students gather on smoke breaks.

Industry observers note that but in between those more experimental moments, it’s easy to see why Grimshaw walked away with the prize, H&M’s first time awarding it since 2020. While fodder for celebrity placements and red carpets, her work also carries “hanger appeal,” clothes that are both wearable and appealing but also evoke something unexpected and slightly “off.” Like a texturized, scalloped suit jacket with a taut waist à la the “Latest Look” or the almost wet-looking crumpled silk slip dress done in a graphic, almost watercolor effect.

According to recent reports, the line took cues from the designer’s college years in London (at 18, she moved there from Hong Kong to attend CSM) and speaks to her introspective way of working. “My whole practice is inspired by my grandmother having Alzheimer’s and trying to represent the fading of memories by using everyday objects and to recontextualize them,” Grimshaw told ELLE after the award was unveiled. “I want to remind us not to take the everyday for granted; that’s why a lot of my work is pencil shavings, cigarettes, locks.”.

Next up, the designer will head to H&M’s home base of Stockholm, where she’ll get started on her collaboration with the brand. “This opportunity is going to be a massive help to make my work accessible to everyone,” she adds. “I’m very excited because this collection was not designed with the idea of commerciality. So I’m really interested to challenge myself and also work with other people to see how it can become that.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE Decor editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Sources indicate that putting a refined Italian spin on the Shaker-inspired cabinets that grace so many American kitchens, heritage brand Scavolini slimmed down the classic border profile to make it “lighter and more versatile,” indicates CEO Fabiana Scavolini, a daughter of one of the 65-year-old firm’s founders. “We felt there was an opportunity to take a design language that people immediately recognize and make it feel relevant to the way we live today.”.

Recent findings suggest that part of the upcoming Poetica line, the cabinets feature a beveled ash frame with the recessed center panel in wood veneer, fluted glass, or (soon) lacquer. “Rather than one particular finish or detail, it’s the possibility of creating increasingly individual interpretations of the collection that I find most interesting,” she states. “Today, personalization goes far beyond choosing a color or material—it means giving homeowners and design professionals the tools to shape a space around different tastes, lifestyles and architectural contexts.”.

The response from clients and designers has already been positive. “What resonates is its ability to add warmth and character while still feeling contemporary,” she notes. “We call it micro-Shaker.”.

Taylor Swift’s Yellow CMA Awards Gown Has a Dramatic High-Low Hem and Ruffles

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that this evening, Taylor Swift returns to the CMA Awards stage for her first performance in 13 years.
  • Swift has one nomination tonight: Single of the Year for her Toy Story 5 song “I Knew It, I Knew You.”.
  • She last attended the ceremony in 2016, wearing a cutout dress by Julien Macdonald:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that this evening, Taylor Swift returns to the CMA Awards stage for her first performance in 13 years. But first, there’s the red carpet, and the singer just made a stylish entrance. Swift arrived at the Nashville ceremony in a bright yellow Oscar de la Renta gown featuring a dramatic high-low hem and ruffled details from the brand’s spring/summer 2027 collection. She completed the look with dangling earrings and gold high-heeled sandals. The singer walked the red carpet solo.

Swift has one nomination tonight: Single of the Year for her Toy Story 5 song “I Knew It, I Knew You.”.

She last attended the ceremony in 2016, wearing a cutout dress by Julien Macdonald:.

In a recent development, last month, Swift was back in Nashville for her induction into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame. During her acceptance speech, she reflected on the city’s significance to her career.

According to recent reports, “I started writing songs when I was a little kid and I knew from the time I wrote my first song that even if it couldn’t be my career, it would be my passion,” she said. “It would be what I centered my entire life around. Nashville is the place that I went to in my middle school daydreams. It was the place where all the wisdom that I wished to acquire existed in one place. All the lessons that I wished to learn existed in this magical place for me. And it ended up being all of that and more. It ended up being everything.

“Fame, that’s sort of a byproduct of my love for music,” she continued. “It’s kind of like songwriter plus Nashville equals fame. It’s why a lot of people know the words to my music, which is awesome. It’s also why there’s sort of like these daily random doses of chaos that just pop up in my life every once in a while, every couple of hours. That can be kind of weird, but I have tools in place in my mind that help me navigate that and get back to true north when life feels so bizarre. Those tools are my memories and the memories that I visit most frequently when I need to return back to some semblance of remembering what normalcy is and why I do this.

Recent findings suggest that “I think back to when I first got to Nashville and I started writing on Music Row. I was lucky enough to get a publishing deal with Sony Publishing when I was 14, and I just hit the ground running. I started writing every single day. I learned so much. I was like a sponge and I have really curly hair and it was yellow, so I kind of looked like a sponge too. But I learned by repetition. I think you truly learn a craft when you do it over and over and over, and that is what the magnificent songwriters that work in this amazing town do. There is no music community like this music community. I know. I checked all the communities. There’s no one doing it.”.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Taylor Swift returned to the CMA Awards for the first time in 10 years this evening, but her husband, Travis Kelce, wasn’t seen there with her.
  • Industry observers note that kelce is in the middle of his football season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Taylor Swift returned to the CMA Awards for the first time in 10 years this evening, but her husband, Travis Kelce, wasn’t seen there with her. Though the singer posed on the red carpet solo, she wasn’t alone during the ceremony—she was spotted beside her friend Brittany Mahomes, a fellow Kansas City Chiefs WAG. (She is married to Kelce’s teammate Patrick Mahomes, and they’re expecting their fourth child together.).

Industry observers note that kelce is in the middle of his football season. His next game is at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, against the Arizona Cardinals, which could explain his absence this evening.

This past weekend, Kelce left the field for part of the team’s game against the Atlanta Falcons due to an ankle injury. Postgame, he gave USA Today an patch. “I’m all good,” he remarked. “I probably could have went more than I did when I came back, but it was the direction the team wanted to go, so I was right there with them. We had a lot of young guys step up, so it was really nice.”.

While he and Swift are supportive of each other’s careers, the pair hasn’t made their red carpet debut at an awards ceremony yet. Last March, they attended the iHeartRadio Music Awards together but skipped the red carpet. Kelce remained by Swift’s side throughout the show.

Recent findings suggest that in an October 2025 episode of their podcast New Heights, Kelce’s brother Jason asked him about being Swift’s creative muse for The Life of a Showgirl. The tight end coyly replied, “I’m just the lucky man that gets to be, you know, the support system for Taylor while she drops one of the coolest albums that I’ve ever listened to, that the world’s seen. I’m excited for her. I’m happy for her. Everything seems to have gone perfectly, all this planning.”.

He detailed what it was like watching her make the album, revealing that he got to listen to it before it was released. “You see it from start to finish,” he stated. “She started this thing in the middle of her [Eras] Tour in Europe. To see it all unfold and come together and her connect the dots—from the strategic planning to how the album was all going to look—then to listen to the music, and everything comes together and her finally getting that 12th song and being like ‘I think it’s done.’.

It has been revealed that “From that point on, it’s like her and her label are just working their ass off to make this one of the biggest releases of all time,” he added. “I’m just happy as hell for it because she’s happy with it. She’s proud of this and obviously I’m proud of her for going through the hoops to live out her dreams.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Republicans in Congress are scrambling to fill as many government positions with unqualified replicants as they can find before the clock runs out on their majorities. The giddyap on these nominations has impressed Democrats as being unseemly. From Nomination Notes on Substack:.

This has resulted in some hilarious testimonial follies and at least one near hooley between the two senators from Texas. On Tuesday, it was a panel full of judicial nominees, and there were some real lulus in there. The Democrats on the committee decided to test the nominees’ independence. Who, they asked, won the 2020 election?

This is just equal parts silly and insulting by now. Just say it, people. Joe Biden won the 2020 election.

The real dustup came over the nomination of one T. Elliot Gaiser, the head of the DOJ’s Office of Legal Counsel, to a seat on a federal district court in Texas. Outgoing senator John Cornyn refused to return the “blue slip” on Gaiser’s nomination, at least in part for the reason that Gaiser is from Ohio, which makes sense to me.

It has been revealed that cornyn lost the Republican primary for reelection to the inexcusable Ken Paxton, who had the support of the president and the president’s poodle, Senator Ted Cruz, Cornyn’s colleague from Texas. So I feel pretty safe in speculating that they’re not prom dates or anything. Cornyn blue-slipped Gaiser. Then, on Wednesday, this happened. From The Washington Sun:.

Sources indicate that turns out that there are reasons enough to be dubious about putting Gaiser in a lifetime seat on any court. From Just Security:.

I will grant you that the draining of Congress’s war powers to the executive branch is a horse that left the barn decades ago; in fact, on Thursday, the Senate killed a war-powers resolution as regards the Iran war. But sooner or later there has to be a test case, and it might as well be Gaiser.

And, yes, Gaiser was yet another person who could not say who won the 2020 election.

Industry observers note that come Thursday, a panel of nominees for an assortment of administration jobs met the Senate Homeland Security Governmental Affairs Committee. Senator Richard Blumenthal once again climbed on the merry-go-round. He went up and down the panel asking who won the popular vote in 2020, and he once again was handed the rote bafflegab. Blumenthal was particularly irked by Michael LoSapio, a former Palantir (!) executive who been picked to head the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Blumenthal changed things up a bit and asked LoSapio if there had been an “attack” on the Capitol on January 6, 2021. LoSapio’s response smacked gobs all over Capitol Hill.

The next two months are going to be such fun.

  • Recent findings suggest that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
  • Pajamas have officially left the bedroom and entered the party circuit.
  • For fall/winter 2026, Sandy Liang’s jackets were refashioned from bedspreads and silky pajama tops were reinvented with major ruffles, then turned into dresses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Pajamas have officially left the bedroom and entered the party circuit. Soft, slouchy, chic, easy-to-wear pieces are everywhere on the recent runways. And some of the most interesting examples also come with a strong, literal interpretation of pajama dressing. But even for those who aren’t as daring, the runways are filled with slips, pajama-inspired tops, robe coats, blouses, and lingerie undone dressing. Luckily, fashion’s pajama fascination comes at the perfect time for occasion dressing season.

For fall/winter 2026, Sandy Liang’s jackets were refashioned from bedspreads and silky pajama tops were reinvented with major ruffles, then turned into dresses. The point of reference was a cross between Marie Antoinette and Kiki’s Delivery Service. Elsewhere, Ashley Williams sent out models wearing dresses with silky bed appliqués inspired by ’80s bedrooms and childhood furniture. Marie Adam-Leenaerdt showed neon reversible robe jackets and hot pink lace sets inspired by the kind of slips one might normally use as underpinnings or wear to sleep. “This season is about making with care. About transforming what already exists. About allowing imperfection. More attention,” stated the show notes.

What these looks all also have in common is that they feel like a fresh kind of pajama dressing through the female gaze.

Recent findings suggest that the aforementioned pieces make a strong case for statement dressing on their own, with little styling needed. But if you want to go in a different direction, there is also ample inspiration from the fall/winter 2026 collections. Loewe, Rabanne, Stella McCartney, and Isabel Marant are just a few of the labels that did slip dressing with lace, embellished crystals, and surprising finishes like wax-coated latex in neon orange. Sheer lingerie dressing with a twist is everywhere you look in the form of lace skirts, lace-accented satin camisoles, and slinky little dresses à la Staud and Doen.

But even the humble pajama top has its place in partywear today. It’s impossible not to notice the many silky, vintage-inspired blouses that pull from the everyday roots of the pajama shirt. Dressed up in vibrant shades of turquoise or trimmed in feathers and paired with It shoes and a statement coat, a pajama top is party-ready even with a pair of jeans.

According to recent reports, designers clearly agree: At Dior’s spring/summer 2027 show, models walked the runway in soft striped blouses that mirrored the classic pajama shirt, redone with pizazz. With relaxed silhouettes, they were styled with rounded jackets worn open, then paired with wildly patterned bell-shaped skirts or metallic-textured pants. It was just one of the many examples of how comfy sleepwear-inspired staples work anywhere.

Dressing for a party means you can take some fun fashion risks. Take inspiration from your own sleepwear and the runway, but think less bedtime, more best-dressed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that last night, I was scrolling through my inbox when an invite to the opening of “Ruloph’s Rooftop”—a holiday pop-up at Chicago’s LondonHouse Hotel, replete with private, twinkling igloos—caught my eye. The event is tomorrow, which serves as a jarring reminder that it’s the season to have all party-ready beauty essentials on standby. After all, at this time of year you never know when Rudolph (or something equally festive) will call.

Just in time, Bluemercury’s Holiday Shopping Party is here, offering tiered savings for up to 30 percent off your final haul. The sale runs from November 19 to 25, offering discounts on coveted items for hair, skin, body, and holiday glam. From Oribe’s cult-status texturizing spray and Dyson’s coveted multi-styler to a Victoria Beckham Beauty blush that will make you look sun-kissed in the dead of winter and Tronque’s firming, plumping body butter, some of the most in-demand beauty products of 2026 are on sale.

According to recent reports, as you stock your cart, just keep a few caveats in mind: First, discounts are not valid on gift cards, spa services, or products from Aesop, Baobob, Bluemercury exclusive sets, Dr. Diamond’s Metacine Instafacial Collection Plasma Duo or Dr. Diamond’s Metacine Plasma + Hydr/O Duo, LYMA, or Vintner’s Daughter. For SkinCeuticals products, there’s a limit of three per customer and a maximum discount of 15 percent. For goods from Charlotte Tilbury, Dyson, Elta MD, Maison Francis Kurkdjian, Oribe, PCA Skin, and Victoria Beckham Beauty, there’s a maximum 20% discount. Finally, offers cannot be combined with any other discounts, coupons, or promotions; nor can they be redeemed for cash or used toward prior purchases.

Recent findings suggest that with that cleared up, there are no rules for how to use the following products to give yourself—or anyone on your gift list—the ultimate holiday glow-up. Party, indeed.

In a recent development, get glass skin for the holidays with up to 15% off SkinCeuticals’ P-Tiox, a “Botox in a bottle”-type serum that smooths, softens, and has won the heart of many a Vogue editor (you can read our full review here). Dermatologists are also quick to recommend anything from SkinMedica, including its TNS Advanced+ Serum, which experts count on for tightening, lifting, and making skin (merry and) bright. For a touch of post-party pampering, the Black Rose Cream Mask from Sisley-Paris smells like fresh petals and makes skin feel just as soft. And while Augustinus Bader’s mineral sunscreen may not be as economical as your average SPF, it’s on sale now—making this the right time to elevate your fun in the sun.

Why not knock out some of your holiday shopping while you’re at it? Decked with a limited-edition charm from French jewelry designer Lauren Rubinski, Hourglass’s limited-edition Ambient Lighting Editor Unlocked palette has already sold out at Sephora—someone on your gift list would be delighted indeed to get their hands on the coveted launch. Meanwhile, Chantecaille’s compact wraps powder highlighter in gold and pearls, turning a quick cheek touch-up into a luxury experience. La Mer’s soothing concentrate is a gift that will keep on giving all winter long, keeping skin soft and calm, while Byredo’s Gypsy Water Hand Cream—which smells of pine needles and juniper berries wrapped in incense—will be the hit of the White Elephant swap.

No holiday-party blowout is complete without a touch of shine, and Moroccanoil’s treatment delivers one with nourishing argan oil and a touch of irresistible, spicy amber scent. For a festive coif that’s both textured and touchable, Oribe’s cult-classic spray is always in style—and rarely on sale—while R+Co’s Picture This Dry Texture Balm tames frizz, boosts volume, and fits in your chicest holiday clutch. Between parties, give your lengths a little TLC with Maria Nila’s Head & Hair Heal Shampoo. The Swedish concoction soothes strands and scalp with aloe vera extract, and it smells like jasmine and linden blossoms. Just the in-shower reset the chaotic season calls for.

‘Tis the season to plug it in and light up—and that goes for red lights, as well as twinkling lights. Take advantage of the Bluemercury sale to snap up Higherdose’s Red Light Hat, which promotes blood circulation in the scalp to increase scalp health and (possibly) reduce hair loss. For face, the Light Salon’s Boost LED Mask uses professional-grade wavelengths of red and near-infrared light to brighten, plump, and firm the skin, while The Skincare Tools’ Contour Sculptor offers a more analog solution for a just-left-the-spa-level glow. Finally, if it’s that post-salon look you’re after, Dyson’s Airwrap multi-styler and dryer has yet to be replaced as the coveted tool to beat.

It’s rare to have a natural-looking, sun-kissed glow on one’s cheeks during the holiday season, but Victoria Beckham’s watercolor-like blush makes it easy to achieve. It’s also rare to find a setting powder that comes in seven shades (and comes with a heart-shaped powder puff), as Charlotte Tilbury’s does. Rarer yet is the chance to score up to 20 percent off items from both coveted brands, but it would seem that makeup lovers’ dreams come true during the Bluemercury Holiday Shopping Party. Save room in your makeup pouch for Tom Ford’s sculpting highlighter duo and Trish McEvoy’s intensely pigmented gel eyeliner—both versatile enough for everyday wear or holiday glam.

Why should fragrant spruces have all the fun this season? Bluemercury’s best fragrance deals extend to a Diptyque candle worth gifting—or saving just for yourself—to scent your space with a woodsy-floral blend of blackcurrant leaves and moss. Or, keep the scents closer to your skin (or his!) with Parfums de Marly’s newly introduced Crécy Extrait de Parfum, also studded with blackcurrant as well as lavender, rose, woods, and benzoin. For something slightly spicier—and just a touch boozier—Jo Malone’s limited-edition Vanilla Scotch cologne is all warming vanilla and scotch accord. And for a head start on 2027’s smoky-fragrances trend, may we suggest a spritz of Bō’s Casa Blanca Parfum? Its mix of creamy minerals, white tea, suede, oud, and tobacco places it firmly in on-trend (and terribly alluring) ground.

Recent findings suggest that polish, tighten, and tone with discounted goods that fit neatly into a stocking—or on a bathroom shelf. Tronque’s Firming Butter is the Newly introduced Zealander’s answer to lax or dull winter skin, with its intensely hydrating mix of biotech ceramides and natural oils, plus ocean kelp and red seaweed to plump and tighten. For more skin-softening courtesy of the finest ingredients from the sea, Osea’s Undaria Cleansing Body Polish packs antioxidant-rich seaweed into a gel-to-milk formula that leaves skin glowy and soft as a mermaid’s mane. Meanwhile, Nécessaire’s Body Retinol is a dermatologist-approved secret for smoother skin head-to-toe, while U Beauty’s Super Body Hydrator puts a high-tech spin on beneath-the-chin skincare with Siren capsule technology that strategically delivers hydration to the areas that need it most.

The Art of Breakfast: What American Hotels Can Learn From Europe

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (784 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that there are few things more revealing about a hotel than its breakfast.
  • It has been revealed that at Gstaad Palace, the grand Swiss hotel, breakfast is, like everything else, a dignified affair.
  • “Guests should feel like they are in their castle or palace, and they should be welcomed like it’s their house and it’s their best friends serving them,” stated Andrea Scherz, general manager, whose family has owned the hotel since 1947.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there are few things more revealing about a hotel than its breakfast. A property can have beautiful rooms and a marble-clad lobby, but the morning meal is where hospitality is really put to the test. And while American hotels have become very good at building elaborate breakfast buffets, there is often something missing: the sense that anyone has given the experience that much thought. Too often, guests are greeted with scrambled eggs under a heat lamp, a few slices of wet bacon, and a $38 bill. In Europe, meanwhile, breakfast can involve silver cake stands, homemade jams, excellent coffee, and a real sense of place.

It has been revealed that at Gstaad Palace, the grand Swiss hotel, breakfast is, like everything else, a dignified affair. The buffet is beautiful but not extravagant, and the selection spans house-made juices, jams, and pastries, eggs cooked to order, and service that runs more smoothly than a Patek Philippe. And yet, despite the formality of the space, the experience feels wonderfully relaxed.

“Guests should feel like they are in their castle or palace, and they should be welcomed like it’s their house and it’s their best friends serving them,” stated Andrea Scherz, general manager, whose family has owned the hotel since 1947. “It shouldn’t be a procedure.”.

Scherz recently had breakfast at an American hotel that left him less than impressed. The food wasn’t necessarily the problem—it was the little things that were missing, the gestures that make a guest feel looked after rather than processed. A hostess took his name, checked it off a list, and asked him to wait while she set a particular table, despite there being an abundance of available tables already set. It was nearly half an hour before he was sipping his humble cappuccino. “They didn’t go the extra mile; they didn’t even go the extra meter,” he recalled.

Industry observers note that that gets to the heart of what American hotels often get wrong about the most important meal of the day: they confuse abundance with luxury. More eggs, more bacon, more potatoes—but bigger isn’t always better. “Great breakfast is often about something less complicated,” remarked Nick Hatsatouris, owner at Caffé Tusk, a European-style café inside the Evelyn Hotel in Newly introduced York City. “A great breakfast is a simple menu with quality ingredients, the ritual of the service, and the atmosphere of the room.”.

There’s also the question of price. In the United States, breakfast is frequently an additional à la carte charge, even at hotels where the room rate can feel steep. At most European hotels, the charge is folded into the room rate in advance; for guests booking through a travel advisor, it is often waived.

It has been revealed that “For American hotels, I think the lesson is about more than including breakfast in the rate,” remarked Amy Brandwein, the James Beard Award-nominated chef-owner of Washington, D.C.’s Centrolina. “It’s about recognizing breakfast as an essential part of hospitality and an opportunity to express a hotel’s identity, its connection to local producers, and its commitment to the guest’s well-being.”.

Beyond price, the best hotel breakfasts in Europe also reflect where guests are. At Gleneagles in Scotland, for instance, the Scullery puts a distinctly Scottish spin on the morning buffet with local charcuterie, house-made sausages and haggis, and freshly prepared eggs and pancakes. There’s a Bloody Mary station, too, as well as undeniably cozy and humble Scottish porridge. Adare Manor in Ireland serves its breakfast of Irish breads, cheeses, and hot dishes in a 132-foot-long gallery. And at Passalacqua on Lake Como, guests can take breakfast in the garden or beneath frescoed ceilings, with fresh fruit grown in the property’s gardens, eggs from the property’s own chickens, and 11 varieties of regional cakes arranged on silver tiered stands.

Industry observers note that of course, not every hotel needs a sprawling buffet or a kitchen turning out elaborate dishes. Smaller, more thoughtful changes can go a long way.

Brandwein remembers European breakfasts for their balance: beautiful cappuccinos, whole-grain breads, oats, flaxseeds, fresh fruit, and excellent local honey. “I find the typical American hotel breakfast rather heavy and unimaginative,” she remarked, pointing to the usual emphasis on eggs, potatoes, bacon, and sausage. She would like to see more whole grains, fresh produce, and lighter preparations. The ingredients don’t need to be complicated; in fact, the simpler they are, the better. Quality and presentation go a long way.

A hotel breakfast doesn’t need 40 items on a buffet or a pastry chef working through the night. It needs good coffee, something fresh and local, and a staff who seem happy to have you there.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you, like most people, hear the term “bourbon chicken” and have no idea what it is, let me call it by its more common name: toothpick chicken. Yes, the suspiciously delicious chicken shelled out at mall food courts on toothpicks is most likely bourbon chicken. Popular at American Chinese or Cajun-style Chinese restaurants, the sticky-sweet chicken is the utter definition of delicious, luring weary shoppers into food courts to find refuge from the bubblegum pink sweatpants and ripped denim. This version takes cues from the classic but swaps in some autumnal ingredients to make it fit for the season. Charred brussels sprouts leaves and pecans add bulk, while maple syrup and apple cider vinegar give it that delightful tart-sweet flavor we know and love. Serve it over rice or noodles or all by its lonesome for a hearty dinner that will take you back to the '90s.

More chicken dinner winners here: Sheet-Pan Hot Honey Chicken and Peaches; Basil Chicken Stir-Fry; and Ginger-Garlic Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry.

Whisk one 1½" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, ⅓ cup bourbon, ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, ¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes, 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce, and ½ cup water in a small bowl to combine. Set sauce aside.

Toss 1½ lb. skinless, boneless chicken breasts, halved crosswise, thinly sliced against the grain, remaining 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, and remaining 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce in a medium bowl until chicken is coated; set aside.

Heat 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add 1 lb. brussels sprouts, halved through stems, leaves separated, and cook, stirring very occasionally, until just tender and blackened in spots, about 5 minutes. Transfer to another medium bowl.

Recent findings suggest that add more oil if pan looks dry and, working in batches if needed, arrange reserved chicken in a single layer and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Transfer to bowl with brussels sprouts.

Add reserved sauce to same pan and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 1 minute. Remove pan from heat and return brussels sprouts and chicken to pan; top with 1 cup salted roasted pecans, coarsely chopped. Toss to coat in sauce. Serve chicken and brussels sprouts with steamed white rice if desired.

#54577. Breaking: Supersized Fashion: The Rise of Giant Bags, Jewelry, and Accessories

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (643 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Elle ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Supersized Fashion: The Rise of Giant Bags, Jewelry, and Accessories

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (643 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that rosalía was recently spotted walking through the Upcoming York City streets with a Dana Toder bag over three feet long.
  • In case there was any doubt, the point of view was the bag.
  • There’s something undoubtedly beautiful about taking an everyday object and making it obscenely huge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that rosalía was recently spotted walking through the Upcoming York City streets with a Dana Toder bag over three feet long. Paired with her vintage pink satin ballet platform heels from Junko Shimada, the massive, hulking bag from the emerging designer was the kind of shocking jolt of life and newness that typical fashion paparazzi shots lack.

In case there was any doubt, the point of view was the bag. Supersized bags are ubiquitous right now: Chanel, Acne Studios, and Bottega Veneta all showcased their own versions for fall/winter 2026, but Toder’s took the idea to a new level with its extreme size and concept. Consider the bags just one of the many examples of supersizing the everyday. Chandelier earrings and oversize necklaces have never been so massive at Saint Laurent and Valentino. Elsewhere, labels like Comme des Garçons, Vaquera, and Givenchy amped up their usual voluminous silhouettes even more for spring/summer 2027. Rising designer Beata Rydbacken is also making the biggest hair clips you’ve ever seen in your entire life.

There’s something undoubtedly beautiful about taking an everyday object and making it obscenely huge. It puts a focus on what some may consider the everyday or mundane and makes it sort of beautifully ludicrous. Dana Toder originally designed her “Baggage Bag” for Krähe, a fashion film by Lili Conzen, shot on 16mm, which will be released in spring 2027. Accompanied by exhibitions in London, Paris, Berlin, and Vienna, which will also showcase the bag, the film questions who gets to be seen in fashion and gives older women the leading roles. “When Lili shared the film’s concept with me, it connected really well with how I see clothes and accessories: as things that go through life with us and hold memories and emotions,” Toder tells ELLE. “I see a woman’s relationship with her bag or her garments as something very emotional and complex. The focus on older women felt especially meaningful when thinking about how those relationships develop over a lifetime.”.

It has been revealed that for Toder, it’s also a representation of metaphorical and physical baggage. The print featured on the big bag combines analog photographs from the ’80s to today, taken by the designer, director, and actresses in the film, and plays a role in showcasing the shared experience across different women, ages, and times. The bag itself was also made with the help of her 80-year-old leatherworking mentor, Shmulik.

“I’m interested in everything that becomes emotionally attached to a bag: the things it holds, the places it has been with us, and how the material changes over time. It might hold an object that reminds you of someone, or the bag itself might remind you of a certain period in your life,” she says.

“We carry all of that around too. I’m always carrying so much stuff, and I love the sight of a woman digging through her bag, with things falling out. I honestly think it’s one of the most beautiful sights. You’re looking for your keys and suddenly going through things that hold so many memories. Some might have been there for two years, or tucked away in your wallet for what feels like forever. I find something very emotional in that everyday moment, coming across parts of your life that you carry without really thinking about them.”.

Seeing the familiar through a campy, oversize lens gives one both feelings of nostalgia and whimsy, and that’s perhaps why we’re experiencing so many humungous accessories lately. In the case of Rydbacken, in addition to her giant hair clips, she’s also made supersized wired earbuds, the biggest studded belt to ever exist, and jumbo pins, with many going viral. In fashion’s current game of scale, the bigger the accessory, the more room it leaves for memory, meaning, and a little bit of spectacle.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A traditional steak dinner can feel like too much for a weeknight: too expensive, too likely to trip the smoke alarm, too fussy to cook to a perfect medium-rare. But cut a steak into bite-size pieces and suddenly it transforms into a quick-cooking protein that’s no more demanding than chicken breast or tofu. Rub the steak with the spices and make the quick no-recipe yogurt sauce a few hours ahead if it’s helpful with time management. To account for the extra liquid thrown off by the spinach as it cooks, the water-to-couscous ratio in this recipe differs from that often found on the back of the bag (or box) so measure accordingly.

More quick dinners this way: Spicy Chicken Lettuce Wraps; Gochujang Chicken Stir-Fry; and Easy Fish Tacos With Spicy Sauce.

It has been revealed that place 1–1¼ lb. boneless New York strip steak (1–1½" thick), cut into 1" pieces, 1 Tbsp. dried oregano, 2 tsp. onion powder, 2 tsp. sugar, and 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl; season generously with freshly ground pepper and toss to coat. Let sit at least 10 minutes or cover and chill up to 8 hours (no need to bring to room temperature before cooking if chilling).

Sources indicate that heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or medium Dutch oven with a tight-fitting lid over medium. Add 1 bunch scallions, thinly sliced, ½ cup finely chopped dill, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until scallions are softened, about 5 minutes. Add 10 oz. baby spinach in 2–3 handfuls, stirring and letting wilt slightly after each addition before adding more, 5–7 minutes total. Pour in 1 cup water and bring to a boil; season with more salt if needed. Add 1 cup Moroccan couscous and stir to break up any lumps. Remove from heat; rapidly cover with lid and let sit 10 minutes.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, heat 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet, preferably cast iron, over high. Arrange steak in a single layer; cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, 6–8 minutes. Reduce heat to medium; continue to cook, stirring often, until meat is just cooked through, about 1 minute more. Remove from heat. Add remaining 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; toss to combine. (Residual heat from pan will cook out any raw garlic flavor.).

In a recent development, uncover couscous and fluff with a fork to separate grains. Spoon into a large shallow bowl or onto a platter. Top with steak. Cut 1 lemon into quarters and squeeze juice from 1 quarter over steak. Scatter thinly sliced cucumber and some dill sprigs on top; drizzle with oil.

According to recent reports, combine 1 cup plain whole-milk yogurt and a generous pinch of kosher salt in a small bowl; squeeze juice from 2 lemon quarters into yogurt. Stir to combine. If sauce is thick, stir in water, a spoonful at a time, to loosen.

Serve steak and couscous with yogurt sauce and remaining lemon quarter and more lemon wedges for squeezing over.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mussels deserve your attention on weeknights. An affordable and accessible protein, they also happen to cook in less time than it takes to boil water. As the bivalves steam, they release a briny liquid, further perfuming the buttery, sake-fortified miso broth. Load up each bowl with a few good ladles, slurping every drop with an assist from crusty bread or warm rice. And why not enjoy the rest of the bottle of sake alongside your meal?

The seafood counter at your supermarket should sell rinsed and debarred mussels, but it’s easy to do at home. Discard any with cracked shells. Gently tap open raw mussels on a counter to see if they slowly close; if they do, those are okay to use. Swish them in a water-filled salad spinner or colander fitted inside a bowl, draining and refilling until water runs clear (give any especially dirty ones a scrub with a sponge). Use a towel to pull off the fibrous beard and set on a towel-lined tray in the fridge until you’re ready to cook.

More seafood dinners this way: Avgolemono Seafood Stew; Spaghetti alle Vongole; and Gorgeous Green Shrimp.

Place 2 Tbsp. scallions from 8 scallions, thinly sliced on a diagonal, in a small bowl and set aside for serving.

Melt 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add 8 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and remaining scallions to pot and cook, stirring often, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add 2 Tbsp. white miso paste and ½ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes (if using) and cook until miso is broken up and incorporated into butter, about 20 seconds. Pour in 1 cup dry sake or dry white wine and stir to combine, then add 3–3½ lb. mussels, scrubbed, debearded. Cover pot and increase heat to medium-high. Cook, shaking pot occasionally, until mussels open, 5–7 minutes (discard any that do not open). Remove pot from heat.

Squeeze 1 lemon half over mussels. Cut remaining 1 lemon half into wedges for serving. Taste broth and season with kosher salt if needed.

Ladle mussels and broth among shallow bowls, then scatter reserved scallions over. Serve with country-style bread or steamed white rice if desired and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

Sources indicate that I am what you might call a problem sleeper. I often toss and turn for hours before falling asleep. Sleep aids don’t work on me (if I’m sick and take NyQuil, I end up with insomnia rather than a deep slumber). I’ll wake up at witching hour and worry about something before falling back asleep. All of this has been known to wreak havoc on my face. After nights when I barely clock five hours, I wake up to dark circles, a duller complexion, and puffy skin. But Augustinus Bader’s The Overnight Restorative Cream works like an insurance policy for sleepless nights.

According to recent reports, skin repairs itself overnight, and just like every other function in your body, it doesn’t do it as well when you don’t sleep. This can lead to inflammation, a damaged barrier, and even accelerated aging (not exactly what I want to hear as a chronic insomniac). While many beauty products have promised to fake the appearance of eight hours of sleep, Augustinus Bader’s latest cream has a unique rosehip extract that mimics the effects of melatonin. While the hormone regulates your sleep cycle, melatonin could also be good for your skin. One study even found that it might have antiaging properties thanks to its ability to protect cells. This cream is also made with both polyglutamic and hyaluronic acid to seal in hydration. There’s cica to calm skin and combat inflammation. And of course, since it’s an Augustinus Bader product, there’s also an advanced form of TFC8, the brand’s proprietary ingredient, which facilitates communication between skin cells for repair and renewal.

Since using this moisturizer, my skin looks clear, toned, and glowy most mornings. While I do look bright-eyed and bushy-tailed when I manage to sleep that long and use this cream, my skin looks just as good when I get six hours of sleep. Or—gulp—five. (Any less and my brain isn’t even functioning enough to examine the state of my skin.) My next trick will be to find a face cream that puts me to sleep, but since products can’t, at the current moment, work miracles (including this one), I’ll settle for one that helps mitigate the effects of a bad night.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, squash and sausage are a heroic autumnal pairing, especially in a weeknight-friendly pasta. Butternut is the easiest squash to source—not to mention easily found peeled and chopped (a blessing for those with more timid knife skills). But other winter squash like acorn or red kuri can stand in as desired. Whichever squash you select, a sharp, heavy chef’s knife is best for breaking down the chunky veg. But to make your life easier, microwave the squash for 1 to 2 minutes. It will slightly soften, making it simpler—and safer—to slice through.

Rigatoni’s ribbed surface and large holes help chunky squash sauce cling and bites of seared sausage and date wedge—opting for a nutty whole wheat variety will only add to this meal’s autumnal earthiness.

More cozy pastas this way: Balsamic Mushroom and Sausage Pasta; Creamy Red Curry Pasta; and Baked Feta Pasta With Green Sauce.

Cook 1 medium butternut squash (1½–2 lb.), peeled, halved, seeds removed, cut into 1" pieces (about 6 cups), in a large pot of boiling salted water until very tender, 12–14 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer squash to a medium bowl. Reduce heat to low, cover pot, and leave on burner to keep warm.

It has been revealed that heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or a medium Dutch oven over medium-high. Add 1 lb. hot or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed, and break up into small pieces with a wooden spoon. Cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, about 3 minutes. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until browned all over and just cooked through, 3–4 minutes more. Transfer to a plate with a slotted spoon.

Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook 3½ oz. Medjool dates (about 6), pitted, sliced lengthwise ¾" thick, in same pan, turning halfway though, until deeply browned, 3–4 minutes. Transfer to plate with sausage; season with salt.

According to recent reports, add remaining 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil to pan. Add 6 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and reserved squash. Cook, scraping up browned bits and smashing squash with spoon to break up, until lightly browned and broken up into a chunky paste (pieces do not need to be even), about 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, return cooking liquid in reserved pot to a boil over high heat. Cook 12 oz. short tube pasta (such as rigatoni) until very al dente, about 3 minutes less than package directions (it will finish cooking in sauce). Drain, reserving 3 cups pasta cooking liquid.

Sources indicate that add 1 cup pasta cooking liquid to squash and break up squash with spoon until a saucy consistency. Add pasta, another 1 cup pasta cooking liquid, and reserved sausage and dates. Increase heat to medium-high; cook, adding more pasta cooking liquid as needed, until pasta is al dente and coated in sauce, 2–3 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1 Tbsp. sherry vinegar or balsamic vinegar. Taste pasta and add more vinegar, salt and/or pepper if needed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the perfect mac & cheese will have you dreaming about its cheesy goodness for days after you eat it. Obviously, the cheese has to be top-notch, but the real secret to the best version is the perfect crunchy topping. My recipe delivers on all of that and more, so you won't even think about reaching for another mac & cheese recipe for the rest of your gatherings. From weeknight dinners to potlucks and holidays, this is the classic side dish everyone will be reaching for.

Recent findings suggest that what People Are Saying:"Always a huge hit with friends and family! This is my go-to if I'm bringing a dish to a holiday dinner with friends. I've rarely had leftovers to take home!" - Zafire_Shadows.

Sources indicate that "This is exactly what mac and cheese dreams are made of. Love the gruyere funk and the mustard powder (so clever!)." - Pastagofer.

It has been revealed that first, you’ll boil the pasta. Start with a big pot of salted water (and I mean super salty, it should taste like the ocean), then add your pasta and cook it until before al dente—I’m talking still-has-a-ring-of-hard-white-pasta-in-the-middle-when-you-bite-in uncooked. You want it to meld and absorb with your cheese sauce in the oven, not turn into mush. Undercooking now guarantees the perfect bite when you pull it out of the oven.

In a recent development, then it’s cheese sauce time, and that means making a béchamel. You’ll start by melting your butter in a pan over medium heat, then sprinkling the flour over the top and stirring everything together until it starts pulling away from the pan slightly. You’re looking for what’s called a “blonde roux,” which has a slightly yellow tint and should smell a bit like baked goods. You don’t want it super dark (so keep an eye on the heat!), but you definitely don’t want it as light as it started.

Next, add the milk in slowly, stirring constantly so you don’t get thick lumps. Want to shortcut this process a bit? Heat your milk ahead of time to room temperature or even slightly warm. You’re going to cook it until it’s thick and bubbly (about 2 minutes), so having your milk warm will help you get there faster. It’s going to get a LOT thicker when you add the cheese, so if it’s still a little thin but you want to get on with it, that’s okay too.

Once you’re ready to add the cheese, it’s very key to take it off the heat before so that the sauce doesn’t start to separate. That mentioned, if you’ve been at it for a minute and are still having trouble getting your cheese to melt, pop your pot back on the heat for just a few seconds to bring the temperature up and help the process along.

Once it comes together, you can stir in the macaroni until every noodle is coated.

According to recent reports, at this point, you could eat this mac & cheese right now, and it would taste wonderful. But! If you want exceptional mac & cheese, you’ve gotta bake it. So pour it into a pan, then get ready for the best part—the topping. To make it, you’ll combine some breadcrumbs and the remaining half cup of Parmesan in a bowl, then add the olive oil and mix it all up. Sprinkle it on top of the mac and cheese in the casserole dish.

Sources indicate that all you have to do is pop it into your preheated 375° oven and bake it until it's golden brown on top. Go ahead, snag a bite before it's fully cooled—you'll really be able to taste all your extra effort.

The full list of ingredients and directions can be found in the recipe below.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking to make this dish ahead of time, prepare the mac & cheese up until step 4, then cover it in your baking dish and refrigerate it up to 3 days (or freeze it up to 2 months). When ready to serve, add the Parmesan and panko mixture, bake, and serve. If baking from frozen, allow to thaw in the refrigerator overnight before baking.

If you have any leftovers, store them in an airtight container in the fridge for around 3 days.

The next morning, she posted her full performance on YouTube. Watch it below:.

She wore an embellished white sleeveless dress with a red skirt and bedazzled matching cowboy boots. Just like old times, she played along with a sparkly guitar. Swift’s performance began backstage, and she sang while making her way down the halls, nodding to fellow country music stars along the way. She was even joined by Keith Urban onstage.

According to recent reports, during a virtual press conference for the Critics Choice Awards earlier this month, Swift spoke about connecting with Toy Story’s cowgirl Jessie, whose perspective shaped the song. She reflected on her own career trajectory and the ways she has reinvented herself as an artist over the years.

According to recent reports, “It’s interesting because being in the entertainment industry, I’ve always just felt like it’s harder to hit a moving target,” she said of people’s changing tastes. “Once people feel like they’ve figured you out creatively and they’ve figured out what you can do, they usually move into the discardment phase and so that would always be where I would try to pivot and if they think you’re going to zig, you zag instead. Rather than looking at something as exhausting and daunting, I look at as just a new adventure. Once I’ve done one thing, I look for something else that inspires me.

“I feel like with Jessie, she’s always going on these adventures and she’s always trying to help someone new and there’s always something she feels really inspired by and some new challenge ahead of her and she takes them on with such fearlessness,” Swift continued. “Except we see her have this moment of crisis in this film, where she does feel hopeless and she does feel useless and she’s saying to herself, ‘Am I a bad toy? Does any of this matter?’ And it’s that moment that just breaks your heart because you’re like, ‘No, Jessie,’ and then you get that amazing resolution—obviously no spoilers—but in the film she reaches a place that was ultimately what inspired me to write the song I wrote.”.
